requirements.text: The ESA sample(s) submitted for approval shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark.
The ESA sample(s) submitted for approval shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the type designation.

An ESA brought to the market as a replacement part does not need a type approval if it is obviously marked as a replacement part by an identification number and if it is identical to, and from the same manufacturer as, the corresponding original equipment.

An ESA sold as aftermarket equipment for installation in motor vehicles needs no type approval if it is not related to immunity related functions (paragraph 2.12.); in this case the manufacturer shall issue a declaration that the ESA fulfils the requirements of this Regulation and in particular the limits defined in paragraphs 6.5., 6.6., 6.7., 6.8. and 6.9.

If an ESA (e.g. decorative or side signalling lamp electronics) is (part of) a light source, the applicant shall either specify the approval number according to Regulation No. 37, No. 99 or No. 128 granted to this ESA, or provide a test report by a designated Technical Service stating that this ESA is not mechanically interchangeable with any light source according to Regulation No. 37, No. 99 or No. 128; without this documentation approval of the ESA under Regulation No. 10 shall not be granted.

ESAs which are intentional RF transmitters (e.g. radar, keyless-entry aerial if transmitting) and which have not received type approval in conjunction with a vehicle manufacturer shall be supplied with suitable installation guidelines.

An approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3. shall be affixed to every ESA conforming to a type approved under this Regulation (no marking is required for electrical/electronic systems built into vehicles approved as units).
The approval mark shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E", followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.
The approval mark shall comprise, to the right of the circle, the number of this Regulation (10), followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number.
Approval markings on ESAs in conformity with paragraph 5.3. need not be visible when the ESA is installed in the vehicle.
The ESA(s) shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
The ESA(s) shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions and for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.
The broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.

When measured by the method of Annex 7, the ESA broadband emission (dB microvolts/m) shall be below the limit of 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band, decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz, and 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz (Appendix 6).
When measured by the method of Annex 7, the ESA broadband emission shall be below the constant limit of 63 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band.
The narrowband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8.

When measured by the method of Annex 8, the ESA narrowband emission (dB microvolts/m) shall be below the limit of 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band, decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz, and 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz (Appendix 7).
When measured by the method of Annex 8, the ESA narrowband emission shall be below the constant limit of 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band.
An ESA that does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.6.2. and Annex 8 (narrowband emission).

The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
The maximum allowed positive transient pulse amplitude emitted by the ESA on the supply lines shall be +75 V for vehicles with 12 V systems and +150 V for vehicles with 24 V systems.
The maximum allowed negative transient pulse amplitude emitted by the ESA on the supply lines shall be -100 V for vehicles with 12 V systems and -450 V for vehicles with 24 V systems.
ESAs that are not switched, contain no switches or do not include inductive load need not be tested for transient conducted emission and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.

The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9 (stripline, TEM cell, BCI, ALSE/absorber chamber, reverberation chamber).

The ESA radiated immunity test severity in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz band shall be per Table 2a for the chosen method: Stripline 60 V/m (20-400 MHz); TEM cell 75 V/m (20-200 MHz); BCI 60 mA (20-400 MHz); ALSE 30 V/m (80-2,000 MHz) and 10 V/m (2,000-6,000 MHz); Reverberation chamber 21 V/m (LUF-2,000 MHz) and 7 V/m (2,000-6,000 MHz).

The ESA radiated immunity minimum test level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz band shall be per Table 2b for the chosen method: Stripline 50 V/m (20-400 MHz); TEM cell 62.5 V/m (20-200 MHz); BCI 50 mA (20-400 MHz); ALSE 25 V/m (80-2,000 MHz) and 8 V/m (2,000-6,000 MHz); Reverberation chamber 18 V/m (LUF-2,000 MHz) and 6 V/m (2,000-6,000 MHz).

During the radiated immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 9, there shall be no degradation of performance of the ESA's "immunity related functions" (e.g. camera/indirect vision, radar/LIDAR braking or blind-spot functions, pedestrian impact sensing, direction indicator, anti-theft alarm).
ESAs with no immunity related functions need not be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.8. and Annex 9.

Loss of function of a receiver ESA during the immunity test, when the test signal is within the receiver bandwidth (RF exclusion band) specified for the radio service/product in the harmonized international EMC standard, does not necessarily lead to fail criteria.

The immunity of the ESA to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested according to ISO 16750-2 for the starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels of Tables 3a and 3b; the starting profile shall be assessed with the functional status classification of ISO 16750-1 and pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b with the Functional Performance Status Classification (FPSC) of ISO 7637-1.

For ESAs that could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started with a 12 V/24 V starter motor, the ESA shall withstand the starting profile at immunity test level II (12 V and 24 V systems), 10 pulses, with functional status B for ESAs related to immunity related functions which shall be operational during engine start phases, C for other immunity-related ESAs, and D for ESAs not related to immunity related functions.
The ESA shall withstand test pulse 1 at -75 V (12 V system) or -450 V (24 V system), 500 pulses, with FPSC III for ESAs related and not related to immunity related functions.

The ESA shall withstand test pulse 2a at +37 V (12 V and 24 V systems), 500 pulses, with FPSC I for ESAs related to immunity related functions and III for ESAs not related to immunity related functions.

The ESA shall withstand test pulse 2b at +10 V (12 V system) or +20 V (24 V system), 10 pulses, with FPSC II for ESAs related to immunity related functions and III for ESAs not related to immunity related functions.

The ESA shall withstand test pulse 3a at -112 V (12 V system) or -150 V (24 V system), test duration 1 h, with FPSC I for ESAs related to immunity related functions and III for ESAs not related to immunity related functions.

The ESA shall withstand test pulse 3b at +75 V (12 V system) or +150 V (24 V system), test duration 1 h, with FPSC I for ESAs related to immunity related functions and III for ESAs not related to immunity related functions.
ESAs that are RF transmitters (e.g. radar, transmitting keyless-entry aerial) shall be tested in the transmit mode.

For RF transmitting ESAs, wanted emissions within the necessary bandwidth and out-of-band emissions are disregarded for the purpose of this Regulation, but spurious emissions are subject to the emission requirements of this Regulation.

If the bumper module's ESAs are active during REESS charging, or the charge-port area includes a vehicle inlet or charging electronics, the ESAs shall be designed, constructed and fitted so that the vehicle complies with the requirements of this Regulation in configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid".

ESAs in configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" (ESAs active during charging, or charge-port inlet/charging electronics) shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions and for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.

In configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.

In configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", when measured by the Annex 7 method, the ESA broadband emission limit shall decrease logarithmically from 62 to 52 dBµV/m over the 30 to 75 MHz band. It shall then increase logarithmically from 52 to 63 dBµV/m over the 75 to 400 MHz band, as shown in Appendix 6.

In configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", when measured by the Annex 7 method, the ESA broadband emission limit shall remain constant at 63 dBµV/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the ESA representative of its type in configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the measured broadband values, expressed in dBµV/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

If the charge-port area includes a vehicle inlet or charging electronics connected to AC power lines, the harmonics emission on AC power lines generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the Annex 17 method. That method is defined by the manufacturer in accordance with the Technical Service.

For an ESA in REESS charging mode with input current ≤ 16 A per phase, the harmonics emission on AC power lines, measured by the Annex 17 method, shall not exceed the limits defined in IEC 61000-3-2 and given in Table 12.

Maximum authorized harmonic current for an ESA with input current ≤ 16 A per phase (Annex 17), applied per IEC 61000-3-2 paragraph 6.3.3.4. Odd harmonics: n=3: 2.3 A; n=5: 1.14 A; n=7: 0.77 A; n=9: 0.40 A; n=11: 0.33 A; n=13: 0.21 A; 15 ≤ n ≤ 39: 0.15×15/n A. Even harmonics: n=2: 1.08 A; n=4: 0.43 A; n=6: 0.30 A; 8 ≤ n ≤ 40: 0.23×8/n A.

For an ESA in REESS charging mode with input current > 16 A and ≤ 75 A per phase, the harmonics emission on AC power lines, measured by the Annex 17 method, shall not exceed the limits defined in IEC 61000-3-12 and given in Tables 13, 14 and 15.

For an ESA with input current > 16 A and ≤ 75 A per phase that is single-phase or other than balanced three-phase equipment, the acceptable individual harmonic currents In/I1 (%) and maximum current harmonic ratios (%) depend on minimum Rsce. Values are listed as I3/I5/I7/I9/I11/I13/THD/PWHD. Rsce 33: 21.6/10.7/7.2/3.8/3.1/2/23/23. Rsce 66: 24/13/8/5/4/3/26/26. Rsce 120: 27/15/10/6/5/4/30/30. Rsce 250: 35/20/13/9/8/6/40/40. Rsce ≥ 350: 41/24/15/12/10/8/47/47. Relative values of even harmonics ≤ 12 shall be lower than 16/n %. Even harmonics > 12 are counted in THD and PWHD in the same way as odd harmonics. Linear interpolation between successive Rsce values is authorized.

For an ESA with input current > 16 A and ≤ 75 A per phase that is balanced three-phase equipment, the acceptable individual harmonic currents In/I1 (%) and maximum current harmonic ratios (%) depend on minimum Rsce. Values are listed as I5/I7/I11/I13/THD/PWHD. Rsce 33: 10.7/7.2/3.1/2/13/22. Rsce 66: 14/9/5/3/16/25. Rsce 120: 19/12/7/4/22/28. Rsce 250: 31/20/12/7/37/38. Rsce ≥ 350: 40/25/15/10/48/46. Relative values of even harmonics ≤ 12 shall be lower than 16/n %. Even harmonics > 12 are counted in THD and PWHD in the same way as odd harmonics. Linear interpolation between successive Rsce values is authorized.

For an ESA with input current > 16 A and ≤ 75 A per phase that is balanced three-phase equipment under specific conditions, the acceptable individual harmonic currents In/I1 (%) and maximum current harmonic ratios (%) depend on minimum Rsce. Values are listed as I5/I7/I11/I13/THD/PWHD. Rsce 33: 10.7/7.2/3.1/2/13/22. Rsce ≥ 120: 40/25/15/10/48/46. Relative values of even harmonics ≤ 12 shall be lower than 16/n %. Even harmonics > 12 are counted in THD and PWHD in the same way as odd harmonics.

If the charge-port area includes a vehicle inlet or charging electronics connected to AC power lines, the emission of voltage changes, voltage fluctuations and flicker on AC power lines generated by the ESA shall be measured by the Annex 18 method. That method is defined by the ESA manufacturer in accordance with the Technical Service.

For an ESA in REESS charging mode with rated current ≤ 16 A per phase and not subjected to conditional connection, measured by the Annex 18 method (IEC 61000-3-3, Clause 5), the value of Pst shall not be greater than 1.0.

For an ESA in REESS charging mode with rated current ≤ 16 A per phase and not subjected to conditional connection, measured by the Annex 18 method (IEC 61000-3-3, Clause 5), the value of Plt shall not be greater than 0.65.

For an ESA in REESS charging mode with rated current ≤ 16 A per phase and not subjected to conditional connection, measured by the Annex 18 method (IEC 61000-3-3, Clause 5), d(t) during a voltage change shall not exceed 3.3 per cent for more than 500 ms.

For an ESA in REESS charging mode with rated current ≤ 16 A per phase and not subjected to conditional connection, measured by the Annex 18 method (IEC 61000-3-3, Clause 5), the relative steady-state voltage change dc shall not exceed 3.3 per cent.

For an ESA in REESS charging mode with rated current ≤ 16 A per phase and not subjected to conditional connection, measured by the Annex 18 method (IEC 61000-3-3, Clause 5), the maximum relative voltage change dmax shall not exceed 6 per cent.

For an ESA in REESS charging mode with rated current > 16 A and ≤ 75 A per phase and subjected to conditional connection, measured by the Annex 18 method (IEC 61000-3-11, Clause 5), the value of Pst shall not be greater than 1.0.

For an ESA in REESS charging mode with rated current > 16 A and ≤ 75 A per phase and subjected to conditional connection, measured by the Annex 18 method (IEC 61000-3-11, Clause 5), the value of Plt shall not be greater than 0.65.

For an ESA in REESS charging mode with rated current > 16 A and ≤ 75 A per phase and subjected to conditional connection, measured by the Annex 18 method (IEC 61000-3-11, Clause 5), d(t) during a voltage change shall not exceed 3.3 per cent for more than 500 ms.

For an ESA in REESS charging mode with rated current > 16 A and ≤ 75 A per phase and subjected to conditional connection, measured by the Annex 18 method (IEC 61000-3-11, Clause 5), the relative steady-state voltage change dc shall not exceed 3.3 per cent.

For an ESA in REESS charging mode with rated current > 16 A and ≤ 75 A per phase and subjected to conditional connection, measured by the Annex 18 method (IEC 61000-3-11, Clause 5), the maximum relative voltage change dmax shall not exceed 6 per cent.

If the charge-port area includes a vehicle inlet or charging electronics connected to AC or DC power lines, the radiofrequency conducted disturbances on those lines generated by the ESA shall be measured by the Annex 19 method. That method is defined by the ESA manufacturer in accordance with the Technical Service.

For an ESA in REESS charging mode, the radiofrequency conducted disturbances on AC power lines, measured by the Annex 19 method, shall not exceed the limits defined in IEC 61000-6-3 and given in Table 16.

Maximum allowed radiofrequency conducted disturbances from an ESA on AC power lines (Annex 19). From 0.15 to 0.5 MHz: quasi-peak 66 to 56 dBµV and average 56 to 46 dBµV, both decreasing linearly with the logarithm of frequency. From 0.5 to 5 MHz: quasi-peak 56 dBµV, average 46 dBµV. From 5 to 30 MHz: quasi-peak 60 dBµV, average 50 dBµV.

For an ESA in REESS charging mode, the radiofrequency conducted disturbances on DC power lines, measured by the Annex 19 method, shall not exceed the limits defined in IEC 61000-6-3 and given in Table 17.

Maximum allowed radiofrequency conducted disturbances from an ESA on DC power lines (Annex 19). From 0.15 to 0.5 MHz: quasi-peak 79 dBµV, average 66 dBµV. From 0.5 to 30 MHz: quasi-peak 73 dBµV, average 60 dBµV.

If the charge-port area includes a vehicle inlet or charging electronics connected to AC or DC power lines, the ESA's immunity to Electrical Fast Transient/Burst disturbances conducted along those lines shall be tested by the Annex 21 method.

For an ESA in REESS charging mode tested by the Annex 21 method, the EFT/burst immunity test levels for AC or DC power lines shall be: ±2 kV test voltage in open circuit, rise time (Tr) 5 ns, hold time (Th) 50 ns, repetition rate 5 kHz, applied for at least 1 minute.

The ESA in REESS charging mode shall show no degradation of performance of the charging function, as defined in paragraph 2.1 of Annex 21, during the EFT/burst tests performed in accordance with Annex 21.

If the charge-port area includes a vehicle inlet or charging electronics connected to AC or DC power lines, the ESA's immunity to surge conducted along those lines shall be tested by the Annex 22 method.

For an ESA in REESS charging mode tested by the Annex 22 method, the surge immunity test levels on AC power lines shall be ±2 kV (open circuit) between line and earth and ±1 kV between lines. The pulse has a rise time (Tr) of 1.2 µs and a hold time (Th) of 50 µs. Each surge is applied five times with a maximum delay of 1 minute between pulses, at phases 0, 90, 180 and 270°.

For an ESA in REESS charging mode tested by the Annex 22 method, the surge immunity test levels on DC power lines shall be ±0.5 kV (open circuit) between line and earth and ±0.5 kV between lines. The pulse has a rise time (Tr) of 1.2 µs and a hold time (Th) of 50 µs. Each surge is applied five times with a maximum delay of 1 minute.

The ESA in REESS charging mode shall show no degradation of performance of the charging function, as defined in paragraph 2.1 of Annex 22, during the surge tests performed in accordance with Annex 22.

For an ESA active in configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the emission of transient conducted disturbances on 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested according to ISO 7637-2:2011 as described in Annex 10. The emissions shall not exceed the levels given in Table 18.

Maximum allowed transient pulse amplitude emitted by an ESA on supply lines in REESS charging mode: positive polarity +75 V for 12 V systems and +150 V for 24 V systems; negative polarity -100 V for 12 V systems and -450 V for 24 V systems.

For an ESA active in configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the immunity to electromagnetic radiation shall be tested by method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9. Testing shall cover the levels given in Table 19a over more than 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz band, and the minimum levels given in Table 19b over the whole band.

Radiated immunity test levels for an ESA in REESS charging mode, applied over more than 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz band. BCI: 60 mA from 20 to 400 MHz (not applicable above 2 GHz). ALSE: 30 V/m from 80 to 2,000 MHz and 10 V/m from 2,000 to 6,000 MHz.

Minimum radiated immunity test levels for an ESA in REESS charging mode, applied over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz band. BCI: 50 mA from 20 to 400 MHz (not applicable above 2 GHz). ALSE: 25 V/m from 80 to 2,000 MHz and 8 V/m from 2,000 to 6,000 MHz.

The ESA in REESS charging mode shall show no degradation of performance of the charging function, as defined in paragraph 2.3 of Annex 9, during the radiated immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 9.

For an ESA active in configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the immunity to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Table 20.

ESA in REESS charging mode, test pulse 1: immunity test level -75 V (12 V system) or -450 V (24 V system), 500 pulses. Required functional performance status class: III for both immunity-related and non-immunity-related functions.

ESA in REESS charging mode, test pulse 2a: immunity test level +37 V (12 V and 24 V systems), 500 pulses. Required functional performance status class: I for immunity-related functions and III for non-immunity-related functions.

ESA in REESS charging mode, test pulse 2b: immunity test level +10 V (12 V system) or +20 V (24 V system), 10 pulses. Required functional performance status class: II for immunity-related functions and III for non-immunity-related functions.

ESA in REESS charging mode, test pulse 3a: immunity test level -112 V (12 V system) or -150 V (24 V system), test duration 1 h. Required functional performance status class: I for immunity-related functions and III for non-immunity-related functions.

ESA in REESS charging mode, test pulse 3b: immunity test level +75 V (12 V system) or +150 V (24 V system), test duration 1 h. Required functional performance status class: I for immunity-related functions and III for non-immunity-related functions.

An ESA intended for "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" only with a DC-charging station whose DC network cable is shorter than 30 m need not fulfil paragraphs 7.13, 7.15 and 7.16. In that case the manufacturer shall state that the ESA can be used in this mode only with cables shorter than 30 m, and this information shall be made publicly available after type approval.

An ESA intended for "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" only with a local/private DC-charging station without additional participants need not fulfil paragraphs 7.13, 7.15 and 7.16. In that case the manufacturer shall state that the ESA can be used in this mode only with such a station, and this information shall be made publicly available after type approval.
ESAs (components/STUs) approved under this Regulation shall be manufactured so as to conform to the type approved, meeting the requirements of paragraph 6 and, if applicable, paragraph 7.

For conformity of production of an ESA taken from the series, broadband and narrowband emission levels shall not exceed by more than 4 dB (60 per cent) the reference limits of paragraphs 6.5.2.1 and 6.6.2.1 and, if applicable, paragraph 7.10.2.1.

For conformity of production of an ESA taken from the series, the ESA shall not exhibit any degradation relating to the direct control of the vehicle that could be observed by the driver or other road users. This applies when subjected to a field strength up to 80 per cent of the reference limits of paragraph 6.8.2.1 and, if applicable, paragraph 7.18.2.1.

For conformity of production of a component or STU taken from the series, the ESA shall show no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions" up to the conducted transient levels given in paragraph 6.9.1 and, if applicable, paragraph 7.19.1.

For conformity of production of a component or STU taken from the series, the ESA's transient conducted emissions shall not exceed the levels given in paragraph 6.7.1 and, if applicable, paragraph 7.17.1.

ESA broadband reference limits (paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1.): the broadband electromagnetic emission of the ESA, measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed E (dBµV/m) = 62 - 25.13 log (F/30) in the 30-75 MHz range and E = 52 + 15.13 log (F/75) in the 75-400 MHz range, where F is the frequency in MHz.

ESA broadband reference limits (paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1.): the broadband electromagnetic emission of the ESA, measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed E = 63 dBµV/m in the 400-1,000 MHz range.

ESA narrowband reference limits (paragraph 6.6.2.1.): the narrowband electromagnetic emission of the ESA, measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed E (dBµV/m) = 52 - 25.13 log (F/30) in the 30-75 MHz range and E = 42 + 15.13 log (F/75) in the 75-400 MHz range, where F is the frequency in MHz.
ESA narrowband reference limits (paragraph 6.6.2.1.): the narrowband electromagnetic emission of the ESA, measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed E = 53 dBµV/m in the 400-1,000 MHz range.
The test measuring broadband electromagnetic emissions from the ESA shall be performed according to CISPR 25, unless otherwise stated in Annex 7.
During the broadband emission test, the ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.

If the ESA is involved in 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid' (e.g. charging electronics in the charge-port area, or ESAs active during charging), it shall be in charging mode during the broadband emission test. The state of charge of the traction battery shall be kept between 20 per cent and 80 per cent of the maximum SOC during the whole frequency range measurement.

For an ESA involved in 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid' whose current consumption can be adjusted, the current during the broadband emission test shall be set as follows: at least 80 per cent of its maximum rated charging/input current for AC charging; for DC charging, at least 20 per cent of its nominal value, or a minimum of 16 A if 20 per cent cannot be achieved in the test facility, unless another value is agreed with the type approval authorities. If the test is not performed with a REESS, the ESA should be tested at rated current.
For an ESA not involved in 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid', the broadband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25.
The ESA broadband emission limits apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS.

Broadband emission measurements of the ESA may be performed with quasi-peak or peak detectors. The limits of paragraphs 6.5 and 7.10 are quasi-peak limits; if peak detectors are used, a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied.

The test measuring narrowband electromagnetic emissions from the ESA (other than ESAs involved in 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid') shall be performed according to CISPR 25, unless otherwise stated in Annex 8.
During the narrowband emission test, the ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
The ESA narrowband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in paragraph 6.4 of CISPR 25.
The ESA narrowband emission limits apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS.
ESA narrowband emission measurements shall be performed with an average detector.

The ESA may comply with the electromagnetic radiation immunity requirements using any combination of the following methods, at the manufacturer's discretion, provided the full frequency range of paragraph 3.1 of Annex 9 (20 to 6,000 MHz) is covered: absorber chamber test (ISO 11452-2), TEM cell (ISO 11452-3), bulk current injection (ISO 11452-4), stripline (ISO 11452-5) or reverberation chamber (ISO 11452-11). Frequency range and general test conditions shall be based on ISO 11452-1.

If the ESA is in configuration 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid', it shall comply with the immunity requirements using a combination of the absorber chamber test (ISO 11452-2) and bulk current injection testing (ISO 11452-4), at the manufacturer's discretion, provided the full frequency range of paragraph 3.1 of Annex 9 is covered.
The test conditions for the ESA immunity test shall be according to ISO 11452-1.

During the immunity test, the ESA under test shall be switched on and stimulated to be in normal operation condition. It shall be arranged as defined in Annex 9 unless individual test methods dictate otherwise.

If the ESA is involved in 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid', the REESS shall be in charging mode during the immunity test. The traction battery SOC shall be kept between 20 per cent and 80 per cent of the maximum SOC (the average SOC in case of multiple batteries). If the current consumption can be adjusted, the current shall be set to at least 20 per cent of the maximum rated charging/input current for AC charging. For DC charging it shall be set to at least 20 per cent of the nominal value, or a minimum of 16 A if this cannot be achieved, unless another value is agreed with the Type-Approval Authorities.

Failure criterion for an ESA involved in 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid': a temporary loss of the charging function during the immunity test is allowed only if there is no incorrect charging condition (e.g. over-current, overvoltage) and the function can be restored by a simple intervention without tools (e.g. turning the DUT off/on) after the disturbance is removed.
ESA immunity measurements shall be made in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range, with frequency steps, step size and dwell time chosen according to ISO 11452-1.

In the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, the ESA immunity test signal modulation shall be AM with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth, unless otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

In the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, the ESA immunity test signal modulation shall be PM2 (pulse modulation type 2) with Ton 3 µs and period 3,333 µs, unless otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

In the 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, the ESA immunity test signal modulation shall be PM3 (pulse modulation type 3) with Ton 500 µs and period 1,000 µs, unless otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

When the absorber chamber test is used for ESA immunity, the test field conditions shall be established with the substitution method according to ISO 11452-2, and the test shall be performed with vertical polarization.

When TEM cell testing is used for ESA immunity, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-3. The method of maximum field coupling to the ESA or to the wiring harness inside the TEM cell shall be used.

When bulk current injection testing is used for ESA immunity, the test shall be performed on a test bench according to ISO 11452-4, using either the substitution method with the injection probe 150 mm from the ESA or the closed loop method with the injection probe 900 mm from the ESA. Alternatively, the ESA may be tested installed in the vehicle according to ISO 11451-4, using the substitution method with the probe 150 mm from the ESA.
When stripline testing is used for ESA immunity, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-5.
When the reverberation chamber test is used for ESA immunity, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-11, using a test setup with ground plane unless otherwise specified.

For immunity to transients conducted along 12/24 V supply lines, test pulse 1 according to ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the ESA supply lines and to other ESA connections which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

For immunity to transients conducted along 12/24 V supply lines, test pulse 2a according to ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the ESA supply lines and to other ESA connections which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

For immunity to transients conducted along 12/24 V supply lines, test pulse 2b according to ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the ESA supply lines and to other ESA connections which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

For immunity to transients conducted along 12/24 V supply lines, test pulse 3a according to ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the ESA supply lines and to other ESA connections which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

For immunity to transients conducted along 12/24 V supply lines, test pulse 3b according to ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the ESA supply lines and to other ESA connections which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

The starting profile according to ISO 16750-2 shall be applied to the ESA's 12/24 V supply lines and to other ESA connections which may be operationally connected to supply lines. ESAs reserved exclusively for mounting on electric vehicles (without a 12 V/24 V starter motor) are not subject to the starting profile.

Transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on 12/24 V supply lines shall be measured according to ISO 7637-2. This applies to the supply lines and to other ESA connections which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

If the bumper's charge-port area includes a vehicle inlet/charging electronics (ESA in configuration 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid'), the harmonics generated by the ESA on its AC power lines shall be tested according to IEC 61000-3-2 for input current in charging mode ≤ 16 A per phase (class A equipment), or according to IEC 61000-3-12 for input current > 16 A and ≤ 75 A per phase.

For the harmonics test of a charging-mode ESA (if fitted), the state of charge of the traction battery shall be kept between 20 per cent and 80 per cent of the maximum SOC during the whole measurement.

For the harmonics test of a charging-mode ESA (if fitted), if the current consumption can be adjusted, the current shall be set to at least 80 per cent of its maximum rated charging/input current value for AC charging.
For a charging-mode ESA (if fitted), even and odd current harmonics shall be measured up to the 40th harmonic.
A single-phase or three-phase charging-mode ESA (if fitted) with input current ≤ 16 A per phase shall meet the harmonic limits of Table 12 of paragraph 7.11.2.1.
A single-phase or other than balanced three-phase charging-mode ESA (if fitted) with input current > 16 A and ≤ 75 A per phase shall meet the harmonic limits of Table 13 of paragraph 7.11.2.2.
A balanced three-phase charging-mode ESA (if fitted) with input current > 16 A and ≤ 75 A per phase shall meet the harmonic limits of Table 14 of paragraph 7.11.2.2.

For a three-phase charging-mode ESA (if fitted) with input current > 16 A and ≤ 75 A per phase, when at least one of conditions a), b) or c) of Clause 5.2 of IEC 61000-3-12 is fulfilled, the harmonic limits of Table 15 of paragraph 7.11.2.2. may be applied.

If fitted, a charging-mode ESA with rated current ≤ 16 A per phase and not subjected to conditional connection shall be tested for voltage changes, voltage fluctuations and flicker on its AC power lines according to IEC 61000-3-3 (Clause 4).

If fitted, a charging-mode ESA with rated current > 16 A and ≤ 75 A per phase and subjected to conditional connection shall be tested for voltage changes, voltage fluctuations and flicker on its AC power lines according to IEC 61000-3-11 (Clause 6).
For the flicker test of a charging-mode ESA (if fitted), the state of charge of the traction battery shall be kept between 20 per cent and 80 per cent of the maximum SOC during the whole measurement.

For the flicker test of a charging-mode ESA (if fitted), if the current consumption can be adjusted, the current shall be set to at least 80 per cent of its maximum rated charging/input current value for AC charging.
For a charging-mode ESA (if fitted), the short duration flicker value, long duration flicker value and voltage relative variation shall be determined in the time domain.
A charging-mode ESA (if fitted) with input current ≤ 16 A per phase and not subjected to conditional connection shall meet the flicker/voltage change limits of paragraph 7.12.2.1.
A charging-mode ESA (if fitted) with input current > 16 A and ≤ 75 A per phase and subjected to conditional connection shall meet the flicker/voltage change limits of paragraph 7.12.2.2.
If fitted, the radio frequency conducted disturbances generated by a charging-mode ESA on its AC or DC power lines shall be measured according to CISPR 16-2-1 unless otherwise stated in Annex 19.

For the conducted RF emission test of a charging-mode ESA (if fitted), the state of charge of the traction battery shall be kept between 20 per cent and 80 per cent of the maximum SOC during the whole frequency range measurement.

For the conducted RF emission test of a charging-mode ESA (if fitted), if the current consumption can be adjusted, the current shall be set to at least 80 per cent of its maximum rated charging/input current value for AC charging.

For the conducted RF emission test of a charging-mode ESA (if fitted), if the current consumption can be adjusted, the current shall be set to at least 20 per cent of its nominal value, or to a minimum of 16 A if 20 per cent cannot be achieved in the test facility, for DC charging, unless another value is agreed with the Type Approval Authority.
The conducted RF emission limits for a charging-mode ESA (if fitted) apply throughout the frequency range 0.15 to 30 MHz for measurements in a shielded enclosure, ALSE or OATS.

Conducted RF emissions of a charging-mode ESA (if fitted) shall be measured with average and either quasi-peak or peak detectors; if peak detectors are used a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied.
Conducted RF emissions of a charging-mode ESA (if fitted) on AC power lines shall not exceed the limits of Table 16 of paragraph 7.13.2.1.
Conducted RF emissions of a charging-mode ESA (if fitted) on DC power lines shall not exceed the limits of Table 17 of paragraph 7.13.2.2.

If fitted, a charging-mode ESA shall be subjected to electrical fast transient/burst disturbances conducted along its AC and DC power lines and monitored during the test, according to IEC 61000-4-4 unless otherwise stated.

For the EFT/burst immunity test of a charging-mode ESA (if fitted), the state of charge of the traction battery shall be kept between 20 per cent and 80 per cent of the maximum SOC during the whole measurement.

For the EFT/burst immunity test of a charging-mode ESA (if fitted), if the current consumption can be adjusted, the current shall be set to at least 20 per cent of its maximum rated charging/input current value for AC charging.

For the EFT/burst immunity test of a charging-mode ESA (if fitted), if the current consumption can be adjusted, the current shall be set to at least 20 per cent of its nominal value, or to a minimum of 16 A if 20 per cent cannot be achieved in the test facility, for DC charging, unless another value is agreed with the Type Approval Authority.

EFT/burst immunity failure criterion for a charging-mode ESA (if fitted): temporary loss of charging function is allowed only provided there is no incorrect charging condition (e.g. over-current, overvoltage) and the function can be restored by a simple intervention without tools (e.g. turning the DUT off/on) after the disturbance is removed.
The EFT/burst immunity test of a charging-mode ESA (if fitted) shall be conducted in accordance with IEC 61000-4-4 only at the severity levels given in paragraph 7.15.2.1.
The EFT/burst shall be applied to the charging-mode ESA (if fitted) on the AC/DC power lines in common mode using a CDN.
If fitted, a charging-mode ESA shall be subjected to surges conducted along its AC and DC power lines and monitored during the test, according to IEC 61000-4-5 unless otherwise stated.

For the surge immunity test of a charging-mode ESA (if fitted), the state of charge of the traction battery shall be kept between 20 per cent and 80 per cent of the maximum SOC during the whole measurement.

For the surge immunity test of a charging-mode ESA (if fitted), if the current consumption can be adjusted, the current shall be set to at least 20 per cent of its maximum rated charging/input current value for AC charging.

For the surge immunity test of a charging-mode ESA (if fitted), if the current consumption can be adjusted, the current shall be set to at least 20 per cent of its nominal value, or to a minimum of 16 A if 20 per cent cannot be achieved in the test facility, for DC charging, unless another value is agreed with the Type-Approval Authority.

Surge immunity failure criterion for a charging-mode ESA (if fitted): temporary loss of charging function is allowed only provided there is no incorrect charging condition (e.g. over-current, overvoltage) and the function can be restored by a simple intervention without tools (e.g. turning the DUT off/on) after the disturbance is removed.
The surge immunity test of a charging-mode ESA (if fitted) shall be conducted in accordance with IEC 61000-4-5 only at the severity levels given in paragraph 7.16.2.1.
The surge shall be applied to the charging-mode ESA (if fitted) on the AC/DC power lines between each line and earth and between lines using a CDN.
Where the lower bumper height at the test position is less than 425 mm, the vehicle's bumper shall meet the flexible lower legform to bumper requirements of paragraph 5.1.1.

Where the lower bumper height at the test position is greater than or equal to 425 mm and less than 500 mm, the vehicle's bumper shall meet either the flexible lower legform to bumper requirements of paragraph 5.1.1. or the upper legform to bumper requirements of paragraph 5.1.2., at the choice of the manufacturer.
Where the lower bumper height at the test position is greater than or equal to 500 mm, the vehicle's bumper shall meet the upper legform to bumper requirements of paragraph 5.1.2.

Where the flexible lower legform test applies (lower bumper height below 425 mm, or 425 mm to below 500 mm at the manufacturer's choice), when tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 1. (flexible lower legform impactor), the absolute value of the maximum dynamic medial collateral ligament elongation at the knee shall not exceed 22 mm.

Where the flexible lower legform test applies (lower bumper height below 425 mm, or 425 mm to below 500 mm at the manufacturer's choice), when tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 1., the maximum dynamic anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament elongation shall not exceed 13 mm.

Where the flexible lower legform test applies (lower bumper height below 425 mm, or 425 mm to below 500 mm at the manufacturer's choice), when tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 1., the absolute value of dynamic bending moments at the tibia shall not exceed 340 Nm; however, the manufacturer may nominate bumper test widths up to a maximum of 264 mm in total where the absolute value of the tibia bending moment shall not exceed 380 Nm (a Contracting Party may restrict application of this relaxation zone in its domestic legislation).

Where the upper legform to bumper test applies (lower bumper height 500 mm or above, or 425 mm to below 500 mm at the manufacturer's choice), when tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 2. (upper legform to bumper), the instantaneous sum of the impact forces with respect to time shall not exceed 7.5 kN.

Where the upper legform to bumper test applies (lower bumper height 500 mm or above, or 425 mm to below 500 mm at the manufacturer's choice), when tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 2., the bending moment on the test impactor shall not exceed 510 Nm.

Where upper bumper parts (grille, decorative light frame, upper fascia) lie within the headform test area, when tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraphs 3., 4. and 5., the HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over two thirds of the combined bonnet top test area and windscreen test area, measuring points in the cowl monitoring area not being taken into consideration (used for monitoring only and not contributing to the one-third/two-third area calculation).

Where upper bumper parts lie within the headform test area, when tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraphs 3., 4. and 5., the HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over two thirds of the bonnet top test area, measuring points in the cowl monitoring area not being taken into consideration.

Where upper bumper parts lie within the headform test area, when tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraphs 3., 4. and 5., the HIC for the remaining test areas shall not exceed 1,700 for both the child and adult headforms, measuring points in the cowl monitoring area not being taken into consideration.

Where upper bumper parts lie within the headform test area and there is only a child headform test area, the HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over two thirds of the test area and shall not exceed 1,700 for the remaining area.

Where upper bumper parts lie within the child headform test area, when tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraphs 3. and 4., the HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over a minimum of one half of the child headform test area.

Where upper bumper parts lie within the child headform test area, when tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraphs 3. and 4., the HIC for the remaining areas of the child headform test area shall not exceed 1,700.
At the time of pedestrian protection testing, the vehicle or sub-system (bumper module) shall have a relative humidity of 40 per cent ± 30 per cent and a stabilized temperature of 20 °C ± 4 °C.
Either a complete vehicle or a cut-body, adjusted to the conditions of Annex 3 paragraphs 3.1.1 and 3.1.2, shall be used for the test.

When tested as a complete vehicle, the vehicle shall be in its normal ride attitude and shall be either securely mounted on raised supports or at rest on a flat horizontal surface with the parking brake applied.

When a cut-body is used, it shall include all parts of the vehicle front structure (including the complete bumper module with all its attachments), all under-bonnet components and all components behind the windscreen that may be involved in a frontal impact with a vulnerable road user, to demonstrate the performance and interactions of all contributory vehicle components.
When a cut-body is used, it shall be securely mounted in the normal vehicle ride attitude.

If the bumper pedestrian impact sensors trigger an active deployable pedestrian protection system, all devices designed to protect vulnerable road users when impacted by the vehicle shall be correctly activated before and/or be active during the relevant test.

If the bumper pedestrian impact sensors trigger an active deployable pedestrian protection system, the manufacturer shall show that the devices (including the sensing/triggering by the bumper sensors) will act as intended in a pedestrian impact.

If the flexible lower legform test applies (lower bumper reference line below 425 mm, or 425 mm to below 500 mm at manufacturer's choice), the measuring points shall be in the bumper test area as defined in paragraph 2.14 of the Regulation.

If the flexible lower legform test applies, a minimum of three lower legform to bumper tests shall be carried out, one each to the middle and the outer thirds of the bumper test area, at positions judged most likely to cause injury, and to different types of structure where they vary throughout the area assessed.
If the flexible lower legform test applies, the selected test points shall be a minimum of 84 mm apart, measured horizontally and perpendicular to the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle.

If the flexible lower legform test applies, the impact velocity vector shall be in the horizontal plane and parallel to the longitudinal vertical plane of the vehicle with a tolerance of ±2° at first contact, and the impactor axis shall be perpendicular to the horizontal plane with a roll and pitch tolerance of ±2°.

If the flexible lower legform test applies, the bottom of the impactor (without launching/protection parts) shall be at 75 mm ± 10 mm above the ground reference plane at the time of first contact with the bumper.

If the flexible lower legform test applies, at first contact the impactor shall have the intended orientation about its vertical axis for correct operation of its knee joint, with a yaw angle tolerance of ±5°.
If the flexible lower legform test applies, a horizontal and vertical impact tolerance of ±10 mm shall apply to the impact point on the bumper.
If the flexible lower legform test applies, during contact between the impactor and the vehicle the impactor shall not contact the ground or any object which is not part of the vehicle.
If the flexible lower legform test applies, the impact velocity of the impactor when striking the bumper shall be 11.1 m/s ± 0.2 m/s.

If the upper legform to bumper test applies (lower bumper reference line 500 mm or above, or 425 mm to below 500 mm at manufacturer's choice), the measuring points shall be in the bumper test area as defined in paragraph 2.14 of the Regulation.

If the upper legform to bumper test applies, a minimum of three upper legform to bumper tests shall be carried out, one each to the middle and the outer thirds of the bumper test area, at positions judged most likely to cause injury, and to different types of structure where they vary throughout the area assessed.
If the upper legform to bumper test applies, the selected measuring points shall be a minimum of 84 mm apart, measured horizontally and perpendicular to the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle.

If the upper legform to bumper test applies, the direction of impact shall be parallel to the longitudinal axis of the vehicle, with the axis of the upper legform vertical at first contact, tolerance ±2°.

If the upper legform to bumper test applies, at first contact the impactor centre line shall be vertically midway between the upper bumper reference line and the lower bumper reference line with a ±10 mm tolerance, and the impactor vertical centre line shall be positioned laterally at the selected impact location with a ±10 mm tolerance.
If the upper legform to bumper test applies, the impact velocity of the upper legform impactor when striking the bumper shall be 11.1 m/s ± 0.2 m/s.

If upper bumper parts (grille, decorative light frame, upper fascia) lie within the headform test area, the manufacturer shall identify the zones of the bonnet top test area where the HIC shall not exceed 1,000 (HIC1000 zone) or 1,700 (HIC1700 zone).
If upper bumper parts lie within the child headform test area, child headform tests shall be made to the front structure within the boundaries defined in paragraph 2.16 of the Regulation.

If upper bumper parts lie within the child headform test area, the selected child headform measuring points shall be a minimum of 165 mm apart (measured with a flexible tape held tautly along the outer surface of the vehicle) and within the child headform test areas defined in paragraphs 2.16 and 2.44.
If upper bumper parts lie within the child headform test area, the child headform velocity at the time of impact shall be 9.7 m/s ± 0.2 m/s.

If upper bumper parts lie within the child headform test area, the child headform direction of impact shall be in the longitudinal vertical plane of the vehicle at an angle of 50° ± 2° to the horizontal, downward and rearward for tests to the front structure.
If upper bumper parts lie within the adult headform test area, adult headform tests shall be made to the front structure within the boundaries defined in paragraph 2.1 of the Regulation.

If upper bumper parts lie within the adult headform test area, the selected adult headform measuring points shall be a minimum of 165 mm apart (measured with a flexible tape held tautly along the outer surface of the vehicle) and within the adult headform test areas defined in paragraphs 2.1 and 2.44.
If upper bumper parts lie within the adult headform test area, the adult headform velocity at the time of impact shall be 9.7 m/s ± 0.2 m/s.

If upper bumper parts lie within the adult headform test area, the adult headform direction of impact shall be in the longitudinal vertical plane of the vehicle at an angle of 65° ± 2° to the horizontal, downward and rearward for tests to the front structure.

The provisions of UN R26 do not apply to those parts of the bumper module's external surface which, with the vehicle in the laden condition and all doors, windows and access lids etc. closed, are at a height of more than 2 m, or below the floor line, or so located that, in their static condition as well as when in operation, they cannot be contacted by a sphere 100 mm in diameter.

The external surface of the bumper module (fascia, grille, lamp lenses, sensor faces, covers, etc.) shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any pointed or sharp parts or any projections of such shape, dimensions, direction or hardness as to be likely to increase the risk or seriousness of bodily injury to a person hit by the external surface or brushing against it in the event of a collision.
The external surface of the bumper module shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any part likely to catch on pedestrians, cyclists or motor cyclists.

No protruding part of the bumper module's external surface shall have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm; this does not apply to parts which protrude less than 5 mm, but the outward facing angles of such parts shall be blunted, save where such parts protrude less than 1.5 mm.

Protruding parts of the external surface made of a material of hardness not exceeding 60 Shore A may have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm, the hardness being measured with the component as installed on the vehicle (comparable measurements being used where the Shore A procedure is impossible).

If an ornament/emblem is fitted: added ornaments which project more than 10 mm from their support (a base on which the ornament is mounted being regarded as part of the ornament) shall retract, become detached or bend over under a force of 10 daN exerted at their most salient point in any direction in a plane approximately parallel to the surface on which they are mounted, applied with a flat-ended ram of not more than 50 mm diameter (or an equivalent method); this does not apply to ornaments on radiator grilles, to which only the general requirements of paragraph 5 apply.

If an ornament fitted outside the radiator grille projects more than 10 mm: after the ornament is retracted, detached or bent over under the 10 daN force, the remaining projections shall not project more than 10 mm.

If an ornament fitted outside the radiator grille projects more than 10 mm: the projections remaining after the ornament is retracted, detached or bent over shall in any case satisfy the provisions of paragraph 5.2.

The requirements of paragraph 5.4 do not apply to gaps between fixed or movable elements of the grille, air intake or outlet grilles and other gaps in the bumper module, provided that the distance between consecutive elements, determined according to paragraph 4 of Annex 3, does not exceed 40 mm and that the grilles and gaps have a functional purpose.
For grille elements or gaps with a distance between consecutive elements of between 40 mm and 25 mm (determined according to paragraph 4 of Annex 3), the radii of curvature shall be 1 mm or more.

If the distance between two consecutive grille or gap elements (determined according to paragraph 4 of Annex 3) is equal to or less than 25 mm, the radii of curvature of the external faces of the elements shall not be less than 0.5 mm.
The junction of the front with the side faces of each element forming a grille or gap shall be blunted.

The ends of the bumper shall be turned in towards the external surface in order to minimize the risk of fouling; this is considered satisfied if either the bumper is recessed or integrated within the bodywork, or the end of the bumper is turned in so that it is not contactable by a 100 mm sphere and the gap between the bumper end and the surrounding bodywork does not exceed 20 mm.

If the line of the bumper corresponding to the outline contour of the car's vertical projection is on a rigid surface, that surface shall have a minimum radius of curvature of 5 mm at all its points lying from the contour line to 20 mm inward, in the part of that zone situated between and in front of the tangential points with the contour line of two vertical planes each forming an angle of 15° with the vehicle's longitudinal plane of symmetry (Fig. 1).

If the line of the bumper corresponding to the outline contour of the car's vertical projection is on a rigid surface, that surface shall have a minimum radius of curvature of 2.5 mm at all points outside the 5 mm zone (contour line to 20 mm inward between the 15° tangent planes).

The bumper radius requirement of paragraph 6.5.2 does not apply to parts on or of the bumper or to bumper insets which have a projection of less than 5 mm (e.g. joint covers, headlamp washer jets), but the outward facing angles of such parts shall be blunted, save where such parts protrude less than 1.5 mm.
The bumper radius requirement of paragraph 6.5.2 does not apply to the bumper cover (fascia); the provisions of paragraph 5 remain applicable to the bumper cover.
If an EV charging flap (filler cap/cover) is present in the fascia: its projection shall not exceed 30 mm.

If a steel or aluminium stiffener/beam has sheet-metal edges on the external surface: such edges shall not be permitted unless they are folded back (by approximately 180°, or towards the bodywork so that they cannot be contacted by a sphere of 100 mm diameter) or are fitted with a shield meeting the requirements of the Regulation applicable to it.

Folds in body panels (e.g. fascia character lines) may have a radius of curvature of less than 2.5 mm provided that it is not less than one-tenth of the height H of the projection, measured in accordance with paragraph 1 of Annex 3.
If movable air intake/outlet flaps (active grille shutters) are fitted: the flaps shall meet the requirements of paragraphs 5.2, 5.3 and 5.4 in all positions of use.

The registration plate supporting bracket/holder provided by the vehicle manufacturer shall comply with the requirements of paragraph 5.4 if it is contactable by a 100 mm diameter sphere when a registration plate is fitted in accordance with the vehicle manufacturer's recommendation.

If the keyless-entry aerial is exposed or projecting from the external surface: it shall be fitted so that, if its unattached end is less than 2 m from the road surface in any position of use specified by the aerial manufacturer, it is inside the zone bounded by the vertical planes 10 cm inside the extreme outer edge of the vehicle as defined in paragraph 2.7.

If the keyless-entry aerial is exposed or projecting: it shall be so fitted, and if necessary its unattached end so restricted, that no part of the aerial protrudes beyond the extreme outer edge of the vehicle as defined in paragraph 2.7.

If the keyless-entry aerial is exposed or projecting: its shaft may have radii of curvature of less than 2.5 mm, but its unattached end shall be fitted with a fixed capping with radii of curvature of not less than 2.5 mm.
If the keyless-entry aerial is exposed or projecting: the base of the aerial shall not project more than 40 mm when determined according to paragraph 2 of Annex 3.

If the keyless-entry aerial is exposed or projecting and, by absence of a flexible shaft or part, its base cannot be identified: the base projection requirement is deemed met if, after a horizontal force of not more than 50 daN in forward and rearward direction applied by a flat-ended ram of not more than 50 mm diameter at the most salient part, (a) the aerial bends towards the support and does not project more than 40 mm, or (b) the aerial breaks off and the remaining part shows no sharp or dangerous part contactable by the 100 mm sphere and does not project more than 40 mm.
Series-production bumper modules shall be so manufactured that the vehicle conforms to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraphs 5 and 6.

The height H of the projection of folds in body panels shall be determined graphically by reference to the circumference of a 165 mm diameter circle internally tangential to the external outline of the external surface at the section checked. H is the maximum distance, measured along a straight line through the centre of the 165 mm circle, between the circumference of that circle and the external contour of the projection (Annex 3, Fig. 1).

Where a 100 mm diameter circle cannot contact externally part of the external outline of the external surface at the section considered, the surface outline in this area shall be taken as the circumference of the 100 mm diameter circle between its tangent points with the external outline when determining the height of fold projections (Annex 3, Fig. 2).
The manufacturer shall provide drawings of the necessary sections through the external surface (e.g. the bumper fascia and body-panel folds) to allow the height of the projections to be measured.

The dimension of the projection of a component mounted on a convex surface (e.g. sensor faces, lamp lenses, aerial, charging flap) may be determined either directly or by reference to a drawing of an appropriate section of the component in its installed condition.

If the dimension of the projection of a component mounted on a surface other than convex cannot be determined by simple measurement, it shall be determined as the maximum variation of the distance of the centre of a 100 mm diameter sphere from the nominal line of the panel when the sphere is moved over and kept in constant contact with that component (Annex 3, Fig. 3).

The dimension of a gap or space between elements of a grille shall be determined as the distance between two planes passing through the points of contact of the sphere and perpendicular to the line joining those points of contact (Annex 3, Figs. 5 and 6).

The lighting and light-signalling devices on the bumper shall be so fitted that, under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which they may be subjected, they retain the characteristics prescribed by UN R48 and enable the vehicle to comply with the requirements of UN R48.
It shall not be possible for the lamps fitted in the bumper to be inadvertently maladjusted.

If the bumper integrates main-beam headlamps, dipped-beam headlamps or front fog lamps (illuminating lamps of paragraphs 2.5.1., 2.5.2. and 2.5.10.), these lamps shall be so installed that correct adjustment of their orientation can easily be carried out.

For all light-signalling devices, including those mounted on the side panels, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3°.

For side-marker lamps (and side retro-reflectors, if integrated), the reference axis when fitted to the vehicle shall be perpendicular to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3°.

For all light-signalling devices other than side retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps (e.g. front position lamp, daytime running lamp, direction-indicator lamp, if provided), the reference axis when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3°.
Any specific instructions as regards fitting of the light-signalling devices laid down by the manufacturer shall be complied with.

In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the lamps shall be verified with the vehicle unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the condition defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2.

In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair (e.g. left and right side signalling lamps) shall be fitted to the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane, based on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp and not on the edge of its illuminating surface.

In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane; this requirement is not valid with regard to the interior structure of the lamp.
In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics; this does not apply to a matched pair of a function and/or an AFS.
If lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo are fitted, only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo can be fitted on the front of the vehicle.
If lamps incorporating a logo are fitted, all logos that are not vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer logos are prohibited.

Lamps may be grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with one another provided that all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and other requirements, if any, are fulfilled.

Where a lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with other functions, its photometric and colorimetric requirements shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which it is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF; however, when a front position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other functions which can be switched ON together with it, the colour requirements of each of these other functions shall be fulfilled when the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the front position lamp are switched ON.

A single lamp as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1.(a) whose apparent surface is composed of two or more distinct parts (e.g. a segmented LED strip) shall be installed such that either (a) the total area of the projection of the distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis, on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis, occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing that projection, or (b) the minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts, measured perpendicularly to the reference axis, does not exceed 75 mm. These requirements do not apply to a single retro-reflector.

If a single lamp as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1.(b) or (c) is composed of two lamps marked "D" or two independent retro-reflectors, it shall be installed such that either (a) the projection of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of the two lamps or retro-reflectors occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing these projections, or (b) the minimum distance between the facing edges of the apparent surfaces, measured perpendicularly to the reference axis, does not exceed 75 mm.

If the lamp is an interdependent lamp system (single lamp as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1.(d)), it shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.; two or more lamps or separate apparent surfaces in the same lamp body and/or with a common outer lens are not considered an interdependent lamp system, but a lamp in the shape of a band or strip may be part of an interdependent lamp system.
Where two lamps or an even number of lamps in the shape of a band or strip are used as a single lamp, they shall be placed symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle.

Where two lamps or an even number of lamps in the shape of a band or strip are used as a single lamp, they shall extend on both sides to within at least 0.4 m of the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
Where two lamps or an even number of lamps in the shape of a band or strip are used as a single lamp, they shall be not less than 0.8 m long.
Where lamps in the shape of a band or strip are used as a single lamp, the illumination of such a surface shall be provided by not less than two light sources placed as close as possible to the ends.

Where lamps in the shape of a band or strip are used as a single lamp, the light-emitting surface may be constituted by a number of juxtaposed elements on condition that these individual light-emitting surfaces, when projected on a transverse plane, fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.

The maximum height of a lamp above the ground shall be measured from the highest point and the minimum height from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis; where the height clearly meets the requirements, the exact edges of the surface need not be determined.
For the purposes of reducing the geometric visibility angles, the position of a lamp with regard to height above the ground shall be measured from the H plane.

If a dipped-beam headlamp is integrated, its minimum height in relation to the ground is measured from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis independent of its utilization.

The position of a lamp as regards width shall be determined from the edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis furthest from the median longitudinal plane when referred to the overall width, and from the inner edges of the apparent surface when referred to the distance between lamps; where the position clearly meets the requirements, the exact edges need not be determined.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface) of a lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.
If the side signalling lamp functions as a direction-indicator lamp, it shall be a flashing lamp.
Amber side-marker lamps complying with paragraph 6.18.7. shall be flashing lamps.

The photometric characteristics of any lamp may vary (a) in relation to the ambient light, (b) as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, or (c) when the lamp is being used to provide another lighting function, provided that any variation is in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.

If the lamp is a front direction-indicator lamp of category 1, 1a or 1b with sequential activation, its photometric characteristics may be varied during a flash by sequential activation of light sources as specified in paragraph 5.6. of UN Regulation No. 6 or paragraph 5.6.11. of UN Regulation No. [LSD].
White light emitted by a lamp fitted on the front of the vehicle (e.g. front position lamp, daytime running lamp, decorative grille lighting) shall not be visible from the rear of the vehicle.

There shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a white lamp (other than reversing lamps and white side conspicuity markings) if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 2 in a transverse plane situated 25 m behind the vehicle (see Annex 4).

In case of doubt, the requirement on white light towards the rear shall be deemed fulfilled if the luminous intensity of the white light emitted to the rear, as verified during type approval of the lamp, is not more than 0.25 cd per lamp, taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.

The electrical connections shall be such that the front and rear position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps (if they exist), the side-marker lamps (if they exist) and the rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously; this does not apply while (a) front and rear position lamps, and side-marker lamps combined or reciprocally incorporated with them, are switched ON as parking lamps, (b) side-marker lamps flash in conjunction with direction indicators, (c) daytime running lamps are switched ON, or (d) the front position lamp function is substituted under paragraph 5.12.1.
In the case of an interdependent lamp system, all light sources shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.

If main-beam headlamps, dipped-beam headlamps or front fog lamps are integrated, their electrical connections shall be such that they cannot be switched ON unless the lamps referred to in paragraph 5.11. are also switched ON; this does not apply to main-beam or dipped-beam headlamps when their luminous warnings consist of intermittent lighting up at short intervals of the main-beam or dipped-beam headlamp or alternate lighting up at short intervals of the main-beam and dipped-beam headlamps.
Where a closed-circuit tell-tale is prescribed by UN R48 for a function of the bumper lamps, it may be replaced by an "operating" tell-tale.
The concealment of lamps shall be prohibited, with the exception of main-beam headlamps, dipped-beam headlamps and front fog lamps, which may be concealed when they are not in use.

If concealable headlamps or front fog lamps are fitted, in the event of any failure affecting the operation of the concealment device(s) the lamps shall remain in the position of use, if already in use, or shall be capable of being moved into the position of use without the aid of tools.

If concealable lamps are fitted, it shall be possible to move the lamps into the position of use and to switch them ON by means of a single control, without excluding the possibility of moving them into the position of use without switching them ON; in the case of grouped main-beam and dipped-beam headlamps, this control is required only to activate the dipped-beam headlamps.
If concealable lamps are fitted, it shall not be possible deliberately, from the driver's seat, to stop the movement of switched ON lamps before they reach the position of use.
If concealable lamps are fitted and there is a danger of dazzling other road users by the movement of the lamps, they may light up only when they have reached their position of use.

If concealable headlamps are fitted, when the concealment device has a temperature of -30 °C to +50 °C the headlamps shall be capable of reaching the position of use within three seconds of initial operation of the control.
Main-beam headlamp (if integrated): colour of light emitted shall be white.
Dipped-beam headlamp (if integrated): colour of light emitted shall be white.
Front fog lamp (if integrated): colour of light emitted shall be white or selective yellow.
Direction-indicator lamp (if the side signalling lamp provides this function): colour of light emitted shall be amber.
Front position lamp (if provided, e.g. by the grille-surround or side lamp): colour of light emitted shall be white.
Parking lamp (if provided): colour of light emitted shall be white in front, or amber if reciprocally incorporated in the side direction-indicator lamps or in the side-marker lamps.
Side-marker lamp: colour of light emitted shall be amber (only the rearmost side-marker lamp can be red when grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with specified rear lamps).
End-outline marker lamp (if provided): colour of light emitted shall be white in front.
Daytime running lamp (if provided): colour of light emitted shall be white.
Front retro-reflector, non-triangular (if integrated): colour shall be identical to incident light (white or colourless).
Side retro-reflector, non-triangular (if integrated): colour shall be amber.
Cornering lamp (if integrated): colour of light emitted shall be white.

Exterior courtesy lamp (if integrated): colour of light emitted shall be white and, in addition, in accordance with the individual specifications applicable to the specific lamp used for the exterior courtesy lamp.
Manoeuvring lamp (if integrated): colour of light emitted shall be white.
The number of lamps mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of UN R48.
With the exception of retro-reflectors, a lamp even bearing an approval mark is deemed not to be present when it cannot be made to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse.

If the lamps are approved with replaceable light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 37 (not used as non-replaceable light sources), they shall be fitted in the vehicle in such a way that the light source can be correctly replaced without the need for expert assistance and without the need for special tools other than those provided with the vehicle by the manufacturer.
If the lamps are approved with replaceable light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 37, a detailed description of the procedure for replacement shall be provided with the vehicle.
Where a light source module includes a holder for an approved replaceable light source according to UN Regulation No. 37, this light source shall be replaceable as required in paragraph 5.23.

For front position lamps (and main-/dipped-beam headlamps, if integrated) tested at approval with a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, in a secondary operating mode or at a voltage requested by the applicant, the voltage supplied at the device terminals, with the vehicle electrical system in a constant voltage operating condition, shall not exceed the voltage specified for the device or function as approved; this does not apply to devices which include an electronic light source control gear, or a variable intensity control being part of the device, or only light sources approved according to UN Regulation No. 128.

For front position lamps (and main-/dipped-beam headlamps, if integrated) in power supply conditions not covered by paragraph 5.27.1., the voltage at the terminals of the device(s) or function(s), with the vehicle electrical system in a constant voltage operating condition, shall not exceed 6.75 V (6 V systems), 13.5 V (12 V systems) or 28 V (24 V systems) by more than 3 per cent; this does not apply to devices which include an electronic light source control gear, or a variable intensity control being part of the device, or only light sources approved according to UN Regulation No. 128.
The means of controlling the maximum voltage at the terminals of the device may be located within the body of the device.

There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of the lamp observed from infinity; however, no account is taken of obstacles if they were already present when the lamp was type-approved.

If, when the lamp is installed, any part of its apparent surface is hidden by further parts of the vehicle (e.g. fascia or grille), proof shall be furnished that the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles still conforms to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.

When the vertical angle of geometric visibility below the horizontal may be reduced to 5° (lamp at less than 750 mm above the ground measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the photometric field of measurements of the installed optical unit may be reduced to 5° below the horizontal.
In the case of an interdependent lamp system, the geometric visibility requirements shall be fulfilled when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
An LED module does not need to be replaceable, if so stated in the communication sheet of the component type approval.
