All lamps installed on the vehicle shall, where applicable, be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations as specified in the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 6 of UN R48.
If a light-signalling lamp incorporates a manufacturer logo, the lamp shall be type approved according to the requirements of UN Regulation No. 148.

Lamps approved for one or more replaceable light source categories according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 or 128 shall be fitted with light sources approved according to these light source categories only; this does not concern light source modules, LED modules and non-replaceable light sources, except when they are required to be approved by the applicable Regulation.

A device type approved according to any preceding series of amendments to UN Regulations Nos. 148, 149 and/or 150 is deemed equivalent to one approved according to the latest series when the change indexes related to each individual lamp (function) do not differ, and may then be fitted without any update of the device type approval documents and device markings.
If lamps approved for and equipped with LED substitute light source(s) are used, this is allowed exclusively where the statement indicated in paragraph 3.2.8. is present and positive.

If lamps approved for and equipped with LED substitute light source(s) are used, the lamps shall bear the marking related to the use of LED substitute light source(s), checked at type approval and in conformity of production verification.

If the bumper integrates main-beam headlamps, two main-beam headlamps shall be type approved according to Class B of the 01 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 149; optionally one or two additional pairs may be type approved according to Classes A, B or RA of the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 149.

If the bumper integrates main-beam headlamps, they shall be positioned at the front of the vehicle; this is deemed satisfied if the light emitted does not cause discomfort to the driver either directly or indirectly through the devices for indirect vision and/or other reflecting surfaces of the vehicle.

If the bumper integrates main-beam headlamps, the visibility of the illuminating surface, including areas which do not appear illuminated, shall be ensured within a divergent space defined by generating lines based on the perimeter of the illuminating surface forming an angle of not less than 5° with the axis of reference of the headlamp, the origin being the perimeter of the projection of the illuminating surface on a transverse plane tangent to the foremost part of the headlamp lens.
If the bumper integrates main-beam headlamps, they shall be oriented towards the front; not more than one main-beam headlamp on each side of the vehicle may swivel to produce bend lighting.

If the bumper integrates main-beam headlamps, except when used to give intermittent luminous warnings at short intervals, the main-beam headlamps may be switched ON only when the dipped-beam headlamps are manually activated or the conditions for automatic switching ON of dipped-beam headlamps exist.

If the bumper integrates main-beam headlamps, they shall be switched OFF automatically when the dipped-beam headlamps are manually deactivated or the conditions for automatic switching ON of dipped-beam headlamps cease to exist.

If the bumper integrates main-beam headlamps, it shall always be possible to switch the main-beam headlamps ON and OFF manually and to manually deactivate their automatic control, the switching OFF and deactivation of automatic control being by a simple and immediate manual operation without use of sub-menus.

If the bumper integrates main-beam headlamps, they may be switched ON simultaneously or in pairs; for changing over from dipped to main beam at least one pair shall be switched ON, and for changing over from main to dipped beam all main-beam headlamps shall be switched OFF simultaneously.

If the bumper integrates auxiliary driving-beam(s) class RA, they shall only be switched ON together with the driving-beams of another class, except when one or more pairs are used to produce light signals consisting of intermittent switching ON at short intervals (paragraph 5.12.).
If the bumper integrates main-beam headlamps, a closed-circuit tell-tale is mandatory.

If the bumper integrates main-beam headlamps, the reference value corresponding to the aggregate maximum intensity of the main-beam headlamps which can be switched ON simultaneously, obtained by adding the reference marks indicated on the headlamps, shall not exceed 100.

If the camera is used as sensor for automatic control of the main-beam headlamps, the sensor system shall be capable of detecting and reacting to (a) ambient lighting conditions, (b) the light emitted by the front lighting and front light-signalling devices of oncoming vehicles, and (c) the light emitted by the rear light-signalling devices of preceding vehicles (vehicles of categories L, M, N, O, T and bicycles with retro-reflectors and switched-ON lamps); additional sensor functions are allowed.

If the main-beam control is automatic (camera used as sensor), an indication shall be provided to the driver that the automatic control of the main-beam function is activated, and it shall remain displayed as long as the automatic operation is activated.

If the camera is used as sensor for automatic main-beam control, the minimum field in which the sensor is able to detect light emitted from other vehicles shall extend horizontally 15° to the left and 15° to the right, measured from the centre of the sensor aperture relative to a horizontal line through its centre parallel to the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle.

If the camera is used as sensor for automatic main-beam control, the minimum vertical detection field shall be 5° upward and downward 2° for a sensor mounting height (centre of aperture above ground) less than 2 m, 2° to 5° for a mounting height between 1.5 m and 2.5 m, and 5° for a mounting height greater than 2.0 m.

If the camera is used as sensor for automatic main-beam control, the sensor system shall be able to detect on a straight level road: (a) an oncoming power driven vehicle at a distance of at least 400 m; (b) a preceding power driven vehicle or vehicle-trailer combination at at least 100 m; (c) an oncoming bicycle at at least 75 m, represented by a white lamp of 150 cd with a light emitting area of 10 cm² ± 3 cm² at 0.8 m above ground; with the oncoming and preceding vehicles having position lamps (if applicable) and dipped-beam headlamps switched ON for (a) and (b).
If the camera is used as sensor for automatic main-beam control, the automatic transition from main-beam to dipped-beam and vice versa shall not cause discomfort, distraction or glare.

If the camera is used as sensor for automatic main-beam control, the overall performance of the automatic control shall be verified by simulation or other accepted means and by a test drive according to paragraph 1 of Annex 12, without obvious malfunctioning (e.g. excessive angular movement or flicker).

If the camera is used as sensor for automatic main-beam control, the main-beam headlamps may be switched ON automatically only when no vehicles are detected within the fields and distances of paragraphs 6.1.9.3.1.1. and 6.1.9.3.1.2. and the detected ambient lighting levels are as prescribed in paragraph 6.1.9.3.5.

If main-beam headlamps are switched ON automatically, they shall be switched OFF automatically when oncoming or preceding vehicles are detected within the fields and distances according to paragraphs 6.1.9.3.1.1. and 6.1.9.3.1.2.

If main-beam headlamps are switched ON automatically, they shall be switched OFF automatically when the illuminance produced by ambient lighting conditions exceeds 7,000 lx, measured if necessary on a horizontal surface with a cosine corrected sensor at the same height as the mounting position of the sensor on the vehicle.
If the bumper integrates dipped-beam headlamps, two dipped-beam headlamps type approved according to Class C of the 01 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 149 shall be fitted.

If the bumper integrates dipped-beam headlamps, the edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall be not more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle (the 600 mm minimum separation of the inner edges does not apply to M1 vehicles).
If the bumper integrates dipped-beam headlamps, they shall be not less than 500 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground.

If the bumper integrates dipped-beam headlamps, they shall be at the front of the vehicle; this is deemed satisfied if the light emitted does not cause discomfort to the driver directly or indirectly through the devices for indirect vision and/or other reflecting surfaces of the vehicle.
If the bumper integrates dipped-beam headlamps, geometric visibility shall be ensured within angles α = 15° upwards and 10° downwards and β = 45° outwards and 10° inwards (paragraph 2.10.7.).

If the bumper integrates dipped-beam headlamps, the presence of partitions or other items of equipment near the headlamp (e.g. fascia, grille) shall not give rise to secondary effects causing discomfort to other road users.
If the bumper integrates dipped-beam headlamps, they shall be oriented towards the front.

If the bumper integrates dipped-beam headlamps, the initial downward inclination of the cut-off shall be set in the unladen vehicle state with one person in the driver's seat, specified by the manufacturer within an accuracy of 0.1 per cent and within the range defined in paragraph 6.2.6.1.2.

If the bumper integrates dipped-beam headlamps, the specified initial downward inclination shall be indicated in a clearly legible and indelible manner on each vehicle close to either headlamp or the manufacturer's plate by the symbol shown in Annex 7, only the pertinent value being indicated on each variant/version.

If the bumper integrates dipped-beam headlamps, the vertical inclination of the cut-off, starting from the initial downward inclination, shall remain within the limits depending on the mounting height h of the lower edge of the apparent surface (measured unladen) under all the static loading conditions of Annex 5.

Dipped-beam cut-off vertical inclination limits: for 0.5 m ≤ h ≤ 0.9 m, upper limit -0.50 per cent and lower limit -(h + 1.2) per cent; for 0.9 m < h ≤ 1.2 m, upper limit -(h x 2.17 - 1.45) per cent and lower limit -(h x 2.17 + 0.15) per cent.
If the bumper integrates dipped-beam headlamps and a headlamp levelling device is necessary to satisfy paragraphs 6.2.6.1.1. and 6.2.6.1.2., the device shall be automatic.

If the bumper integrates dipped-beam headlamps with a levelling device, in the event of a failure of the device the dipped beam shall not assume a position in which the vertical inclination is less downward than at the time the failure occurred.
If the bumper integrates dipped-beam headlamps, when changing from main beam to dipped beam all main beams shall be switched OFF simultaneously.

If the bumper integrates dipped-beam headlamps, one additional light source or one or more LED modules inside the dipped-beam headlamps or in a lamp (except the main-beam headlamp) grouped or reciprocally incorporated with them may be activated to produce bend lighting, provided that the horizontal radius of curvature of the trajectory of the vehicle's centre of gravity is 500 m or less.

If the bumper integrates dipped-beam headlamps or the camera is used as sensor for automatic dipped-beam switching, the dipped-beam headlamps shall be switched ON and OFF automatically relative to the ambient light conditions according to the requirements of Annex 13, subject to the exceptions of paragraph 6.2.7.5.1.
If the bumper integrates dipped-beam headlamps, it shall always be possible to switch the dipped-beam headlamps ON manually.
If the bumper integrates dipped-beam headlamps, the driver shall at all times be able to engage the automatic operation.

If the bumper integrates dipped-beam headlamps or the camera is used for automatic dipped-beam switching, where the ambient illuminance is 1,000 lx or more the dipped-beam headlamps may switch ON and OFF automatically relative to other factors such as time of day, vehicle location, rain or fog.

If the bumper integrates dipped-beam headlamps whose principal dipped beam is produced by one or more light source modules or non-replaceable light sources or more than one approved light source (unless wired so that failure of one causes all to stop emitting light), a failure tell-tale, flashing or not, is mandatory; it shall be activated, at the manufacturer's discretion, on failure of any one of them or on receipt of a failure signal per paragraph 4.13. of UN Regulation No. 149 (01 series), shall remain activated while the failure is present, and if cancelled temporarily shall be repeated whenever the propulsion system start/stop device is switched ON and OFF.

If the bumper integrates dipped-beam headlamps with light sources and/or light source modules producing the principal dipped beam with a total objective luminous flux exceeding 2,000 lumens for at least one headlamp, they shall only be installed in conjunction with headlamp cleaning device(s) according to UN Regulation No. 45.

If the bumper integrates front fog lamps, two front fog lamps of Class F3 type-approved according to the 03 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 19 or the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 149 shall be fitted.

If the bumper integrates front fog lamps, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
If the bumper integrates front fog lamps, they shall be not less than 250 mm and, for M1 vehicles, not more than 800 mm above the ground.

If the bumper integrates front fog lamps, no point on their apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis shall be higher than the highest point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the dipped-beam headlamp.

If the bumper integrates front fog lamps, they shall be at the front of the vehicle; this is deemed satisfied if the light emitted does not cause discomfort to the driver directly or indirectly through the devices for indirect vision and/or other reflecting surfaces of the vehicle.
If the bumper integrates front fog lamps, geometric visibility shall be ensured within angles α = 5° upwards and downwards and β = 45° outwards and 10° inwards (paragraph 2.10.7.).

If the bumper integrates front fog lamps, the presence of partitions or other items of equipment near the front fog lamp shall not give rise to secondary effects causing discomfort to other road users.
If the bumper integrates front fog lamps, they shall be oriented toward the front.

If the bumper integrates front fog lamps whose total objective luminous flux of the light source does not exceed 2,000 lumens per lamp, the vertical inclination of the cut-off set in the unladen vehicle state with one person in the driver's seat shall be -1.0 per cent or lower.

If the bumper integrates front fog lamps whose total objective luminous flux exceeds 2,000 lumens per lamp, the vertical inclination of the cut-off shall automatically remain, under all the static conditions of Annex 5, between values depending on the mounting height h of the lower edge of the apparent surface measured unladen.

Front fog lamp (>2,000 lm) cut-off inclination: for h ≤ 0.8 m, limits between -1.0 and -3.0 per cent and initial aiming between -1.5 and -2.0 per cent; for h > 0.8 m, limits between -1.5 and -3.5 per cent and initial aiming between -2.0 and -2.5 per cent.

If the bumper integrates front fog lamps exceeding 2,000 lumens, the initial downward inclination of the cut-off, set unladen with one person in the driver's seat, shall be specified by the manufacturer to one decimal place in accordance with paragraph 6.3.6.1.2.1. and indicated in a clearly legible and indelible manner on each vehicle close to the front fog lamp or the manufacturer's plate or with the indication of paragraph 6.2.6.1.1., by the symbol shown in Annex 7.

If a levelling device is fitted for a front fog lamp, independent or grouped with other front lighting and light-signalling functions, the vertical inclination shall remain between the limits of paragraph 6.3.6.1.2.1. under all the static loading conditions of Annex 5.

If a front fog lamp levelling device is fitted, it may automatically adapt the inclination of the front fog beam to prevailing ambient conditions, provided the downward inclination limits of paragraph 6.3.6.1.2.1. are not exceeded.
If a front fog lamp levelling device is fitted, in the case of its failure the front fog beam shall not assume a position in which the cut-off is less inclined than at the time the failure occurred.

If the bumper integrates front fog lamps, it shall be possible to switch them ON and OFF independently of the main-beam headlamps, the dipped-beam headlamps or any combination of them, unless the front fog lamps are used as part of another lighting function in an AFS (with priority for the front fog function) or cannot be simultaneously lit with lamps with which they are reciprocally incorporated.
If the bumper integrates front fog lamps, a closed-circuit tell-tale is mandatory.

If the side signalling lamp (or another bumper lamp) functions as a direction-indicator lamp, it shall be type-approved according to the 01 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 6 or the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

If the bumper integrates front direction-indicator lamps, their category shall be 1, 1a or 1b if the distance between the edge of their apparent surface and that of the dipped-beam headlamp and/or front fog lamp is at least 40 mm; 1a or 1b if greater than 20 mm and less than 40 mm; and 1b if less than or equal to 20 mm (for an AFS, the distance to the closest lighting unit in its closest position contributing to a passing-beam mode).
If the side signalling lamp functions as side direction-indicator lamp on the M1 vehicle, it shall be of category 5 (minimum), category 6 being permitted instead.

Where lamps combining the functions of front direction-indicator lamps (categories 1, 1a, 1b) and side direction-indicator lamps (categories 5 or 6) are fitted, two additional side direction-indicator lamps (categories 5 or 6) may be fitted to meet the visibility requirements of paragraph 6.5.5.

If the bumper integrates front direction-indicator lamps, the edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis farthest from the median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

If the bumper integrates front direction-indicator lamps, the distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axes shall not be less than 600 mm, reducible to 400 mm where the overall vehicle width is less than 1,300 mm.

If the side signalling lamp functions as side direction-indicator lamp (category 5 or 6) on the M1 vehicle, the height of its light-emitting surface shall not be less than 350 mm measured from the lowest point and not more than 1,500 mm measured from the highest point; the upper limit may be increased to 2,300 mm if the vehicle structure does not permit 1,500 mm.

If the bumper integrates front direction-indicator lamps (categories 1, 1a, 1b), their height measured according to paragraph 5.8. shall not be less than 350 mm and not more than 1,500 mm; the upper limit may be increased to 2,100 mm if the vehicle structure does not permit 1,500 mm.

If the side signalling lamp functions as side direction-indicator lamp (category 5 or 6) on the M1 vehicle, the distance between its light-emitting surface and the transverse plane marking the forward boundary of the vehicle's overall length shall not exceed 2,500 mm.

If the bumper integrates direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b or 5, their vertical geometric visibility shall be 15° above and below the horizontal; where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (paragraph 5.8.1.) the downward angle may be reduced to 5°.
If the side signalling lamp functions as a category 6 side direction-indicator lamp, its vertical geometric visibility shall be 30° above and 5° below the horizontal.

If the bumper integrates direction-indicator lamps, their horizontal geometric visibility angles shall be as shown in the figure of paragraph 6.5.5.1. (for the side direction-indicator the dead angle to the rear is an upper limit of 5°, with d ≤ 2.50 m for M1); for categories 1, 1a, 1b mounted below 750 mm the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

Alternatively, at the manufacturer's discretion for M1 vehicles, front direction-indicator lamps and side-marker lamps may meet the horizontal angles of the figure of paragraph 6.5.5.2. (dead angle to the rear an upper limit of 5°, d ≤ 2.50 m), with the inward angle of 45° reducible to 20° under the H plane for categories 1, 1a, 1b mounted below 750 mm.

Under the alternative arrangement of paragraph 6.5.5.2. for M1 vehicles, front direction-indicator lamps and side-marker lamps shall have vertical geometric visibility of 15° above and below the horizontal, the downward angle being reducible to 5° where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (paragraph 5.8.1.).

Under the alternative arrangement of paragraph 6.5.5.2., to be considered visible a lamp (except side direction-indicators of categories 5 and 6) shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 cm², excluding the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light.
If the bumper integrates direction-indicator lamps, their orientation shall be according to the manufacturer's specifications for installation, if any.
If the bumper integrates direction-indicator lamps, they shall switch ON independently of the other lamps.

If the bumper integrates direction-indicator lamps, all direction-indicator lamps on one side of the vehicle shall be switched ON and OFF automatically as defined by applicable UN Regulations and/or by means of one control and shall flash in phase.

On M1 vehicles less than 6 m in length with an arrangement complying with paragraph 6.5.5.2., the amber side-marker lamps, when mounted, shall flash at the same frequency (in phase) with the direction-indicator lamps.
If a direction-indicator lamp is capable of being activated in different modes (static or sequential), it shall not switch between both modes once activated.

If the bumper integrates front direction-indicator lamps (categories 1, 1a, 1b), an operating tell-tale is mandatory, visual or auditory or both; if visual it shall be a flashing light which, at least on malfunction of any of these lamps, is extinguished, remains alight without flashing or shows a marked change of frequency; if entirely auditory it shall be clearly audible and show a marked change of frequency at least on malfunction.

The direction-indicator operating tell-tale shall be activated by the signal produced according to paragraph 6.2.2. of UN Regulation No. 6, paragraph 5.6.3. of the 00 series or paragraph 4.6.1.4. of the 01 series of UN Regulation No. 148, or another suitable way.
If the bumper integrates direction-indicator lamps, the light shall be a flashing light flashing 90 ± 30 times per minute.

If the bumper integrates direction-indicator lamps, operation of the light-signal control shall be followed within not more than one second by the emission of light and within not more than one and one-half seconds by its first extinction.

If the bumper integrates direction-indicator lamps, in the event of failure, other than short-circuit, of one direction-indicator lamp, the others shall continue to flash, the frequency in this condition being allowed to differ from that prescribed.

If the side signalling lamp functions as an amber side-marker lamp on an M1 vehicle less than 6 m in length with an arrangement complying with paragraph 6.5.5.2., the amber side-marker lamps shall also flash at the same frequency (in phase) with the direction-indicator lamps when the hazard warning signal is operated.
Front position lamps are mandatory on all motor vehicles (applies if the decorative or side signalling lighting performs the front position lamp function).

If the bumper lighting functions as front position lamps, their number shall be two, type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

If the bumper lighting functions as front position lamps, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

If the bumper lighting functions as front position lamps, they shall be mounted above the ground not less than 250 mm nor more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm).

Where the front position lamp and another lamp are reciprocally incorporated, the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the other lamp shall be used to verify compliance with the front position lamp positioning requirements (paragraphs 6.9.4.1. to 6.9.4.3.).

If the bumper lighting functions as front position lamps, the geometric visibility horizontal angle shall be 45° inwards and 80° outwards; however, where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

If the bumper lighting functions as front position lamps, the geometric visibility vertical angle shall be 15° above and below the horizontal; however, where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

For M1 vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.9.5.1., at the manufacturer's discretion and only if a front side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, the front position lamp horizontal geometric visibility angle may be 45° outwards to 45° inwards; where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

When the alternative front position lamp visibility of paragraph 6.9.5.2. is used (M1, front side-marker lamp installed), the vertical angle shall be 15° above and below the horizontal; where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

When the alternative front position lamp visibility of paragraph 6.9.5.2. is used, to be considered visible the lamp shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 cm², excluding the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light.
If the bumper lighting functions as front position lamps, they shall be oriented forwards.

Front position lamp electrical connections shall be in accordance with paragraph 5.11.; however, if a front position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a direction-indicator, the front position lamp on the relevant side (or its reciprocally incorporated part) may be switched OFF during the entire time (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the direction-indicator lamp.

If the bumper lighting functions as front position lamps, a closed-circuit tell-tale is mandatory; it shall not be required if the instrument panel lighting can only switch ON simultaneously with the front position lamps, and the requirement does not apply while the daytime running lamps are switched ON.
The front position lamp tell-tale shall be non-flashing.
For front position lamps, a tell-tale indicating failure is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
If the side signalling lamp functions as a parking lamp, parking lamps are optional on motor vehicles not exceeding 6 m in length and prohibited on all other vehicles.

If the side signalling lamp functions as a parking lamp, the number shall be according to the arrangement and the devices shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 77, or to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
Parking lamps shall be arranged either as two lamps at the front and two lamps at the rear, or one lamp on each side.

For parking lamps, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
If there are two parking lamps, they shall be on the sides of the vehicle.

Parking lamp geometric visibility horizontal angle shall be 45° outwards, forwards and rearwards; however, where a front or rear parking lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

Parking lamp geometric visibility vertical angle shall be 15° above and below the horizontal; however, where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
Parking lamps shall be oriented such that they meet the requirements for visibility forwards and rearwards.
The electrical connection shall allow the parking lamp(s) on the same side of the vehicle to be switched ON independently of any other lamps.

The parking lamp(s) and, if applicable, the front and rear position lamps used as parking lamps according to paragraph 6.12.9., shall be able to operate even if the device which starts the propulsion system is in a position which makes it impossible for the propulsion system to operate.
A device which automatically switches OFF the parking lamps as a function of time is prohibited.
A closed-circuit tell-tale for parking lamps is optional; if there is one, it shall not be possible to confuse it with the tell-tale for the front and rear position lamps.
For parking lamps, a tell-tale indicating failure is mandatory if required by the component regulation.

The parking lamp function may be performed by simultaneously switching ON the front and rear position lamps on the same side of the vehicle; in this case, lamps that meet the requirements of front or rear position lamps are deemed to meet the requirements of parking lamps.

If the side signalling lamp functions as a front end-outline marker lamp (category A or AM), end-outline marker lamps are mandatory on vehicles exceeding 2.10 m in width and optional on vehicles between 1.80 and 2.10 m in width.

If end-outline marker lamps are fitted, there shall be two visible from the front and two visible from the rear, type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

Front end-outline marker lamps shall be as close as possible to the extreme outer edge of the vehicle; this is deemed met when the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis farthest from the median longitudinal plane is not more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

For front end-outline marker lamps on motor vehicles, the horizontal plane tangential to the upper edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis shall not be lower than the horizontal plane tangential to the upper edge of the transparent zone of the windscreen.
End-outline marker lamp geometric visibility horizontal angle shall be 80° outwards.
End-outline marker lamp geometric visibility vertical angle shall be 5° above and 20° below the horizontal.
End-outline marker lamps shall be oriented such that they meet the requirements for visibility forwards and rearwards.
End-outline marker lamp electrical connections shall be in accordance with paragraph 5.11.
An end-outline marker lamp tell-tale is optional; if it exists, its function shall be carried out by the tell-tale required for the front and rear position lamps.
For end-outline marker lamps, a tell-tale indicating failure is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
Provided all other requirements are met, the end-outline marker lamps visible from the front and those visible from the rear on the same side of the vehicle may be combined into one device.

The distance between the projections on a transverse vertical plane of the nearest points on the apparent surfaces (in the direction of the respective reference axes) of an end-outline marker lamp and the corresponding position lamp shall be not less than 200 mm.

If a front retro-reflector is integrated, front non-triangular retro-reflectors are optional on motor vehicles, but mandatory on motor vehicles having all forward-facing lamps with reflectors concealable.

Front retro-reflectors shall be two in number, type-approved according to the requirements for Class IA or IB retro-reflectors in the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3, or in the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150.

Additional front retro-reflecting devices and materials (including two retro-reflectors not complying with paragraph 6.16.4.) are permitted provided they do not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.

For front retro-reflectors, the point on the illuminating surface which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
Front retro-reflectors shall be mounted above the ground not less than 250 mm nor more than 900 mm (1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm).
Front retro-reflectors shall be positioned in length at the front of the vehicle.
Front retro-reflector geometric visibility horizontal angle shall be 30° inwards and outwards.

Front retro-reflector geometric visibility vertical angle shall be 10° above and below the horizontal; however, where the retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 10° may be reduced to 5°.
Front retro-reflectors shall be oriented towards the front.
The illuminating surface of the front retro-reflector may have parts in common with the apparent surface of any other lamp situated at the front.
If a side retro-reflector is integrated, side non-triangular retro-reflectors are optional on motor vehicles not exceeding 6 m in length and mandatory on motor vehicles exceeding 6 m in length.

Side retro-reflectors shall be of a number such that the longitudinal positioning requirements are complied with, and shall be type-approved according to the requirements for Class IA or IB retro-reflectors in the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3, or in the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150.

Additional side retro-reflecting devices and materials (including two retro-reflectors not complying with paragraph 6.17.4.) are permitted provided they do not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.

Side retro-reflectors shall be mounted above the ground not less than 250 mm nor more than 900 mm (not more than 1,200 mm if grouped with any lamp(s); 1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm or 1,200 mm respectively, or if the device is not mandatory according to paragraph 6.17.1.).

Side retro-reflectors shall be positioned in length with at least one in the middle third of the vehicle, the foremost not further than 3 m from the front and the rearmost not more than 1 m from the rear (the 3 m maximum between adjacent retro-reflectors not applying to M1); however, for motor vehicles not exceeding 6 m in length it is sufficient to have one side retro-reflector within the first third and/or one within the last third of the vehicle length, and for M1 vehicles exceeding 6 m but not exceeding 7 m one not further than 3 m from the front and one within the last third.
Side retro-reflector geometric visibility horizontal angle shall be 45° to the front and to the rear.

Side retro-reflector geometric visibility vertical angle shall be 10° above and below the horizontal; however, where the retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 10° may be reduced to 5°.
Side retro-reflectors shall be oriented towards the side.
The illuminating surface of the side retro-reflector may have parts in common with the apparent surface of any other side lamp.
Side-marker lamps on M1 category vehicles shall be of the SM1 type; however, the SM2 type of side-marker lamp may be used on M1 category vehicles.

On M1 category vehicles less than 6 m in length, side-marker lamps shall be used if they supplement the reduced geometric visibility requirements of front position lamps conforming to paragraph 6.9.5.2. and rear position lamps conforming to paragraph 6.10.5.2.
On vehicles where side-marker lamps are not mandatory, side-marker lamps are optional and may be of the SM1 or SM2 type.
The number of side-marker lamps per side shall be such that the rules for longitudinal positioning (paragraph 6.18.4.3.) are complied with.
Side-marker lamps shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 91, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
Side-marker lamps shall be mounted not less than 250 mm nor more than 1,500 mm above the ground (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm).

In length, at least one side-marker lamp shall be fitted to the middle third of the vehicle, the foremost side-marker lamp being not further than 3 m from the front; however, for vehicles not exceeding 6 m in length it is sufficient to have one side-marker lamp fitted within the first third and/or within the last third of the vehicle length, and for M1 vehicles exceeding 6 m but not exceeding 7 m it is sufficient to have one side-marker lamp fitted not further than 3 m from the front and one within the last third of the vehicle length.

For vehicles exceeding 6 m in length (other than covered by the M1 6–7 m relaxation), the distance between two adjacent side-marker lamps shall not exceed 3 m, which may be increased to 4 m if the structure, design or operational use of the vehicle makes compliance impossible.
For vehicles exceeding 6 m in length (other than covered by the M1 6–7 m relaxation), the distance between the rearmost side-marker lamp and the rear of the vehicle shall not exceed 1 m.

Side-marker lamps shall have a horizontal geometric visibility angle of 45° to the front and to the rear; however, for vehicles on which installation of side-marker lamps is optional this value may be reduced to 30°.

If side-marker lamps are used to supplement the reduced geometric visibility of front and rear direction-indicator lamps conforming to paragraph 6.5.5.2. and/or position lamps conforming to paragraphs 6.9.5.2. and 6.10.5.2., their horizontal geometric visibility angles shall be 45° towards the front and rear ends of the vehicle and 30° towards the centre of the vehicle.

Side-marker lamps shall have a vertical geometric visibility angle of 10° above and below the horizontal; however, where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle may be reduced to 5°.
Side-marker lamps shall be oriented towards the side.

On M1 category vehicles less than 6 m in length, amber side-marker lamps may be wired to flash, provided that this flashing is in phase and at the same frequency with the direction-indicator lamps on the same side of the vehicle.
A tell-tale for side-marker lamps is optional; if it exists, its function shall be carried out by the tell-tale required for the front and rear position lamps.
A tell-tale indicating failure of the side-marker lamps is mandatory if required by the component regulation.

When an optional side-marker lamp is grouped or combined with a position lamp that is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with the direction indicator, the electrical connection of the side-marker lamp on the relevant side of the vehicle may be such that it is switched OFF during the entire period (both ON and OFF cycle) of activation of the direction-indicator lamp.
Where the bumper lighting performs the daytime running lamp function: daytime running lamps are mandatory on motor vehicles.

Where the bumper lighting performs the daytime running lamp function: the number of daytime running lamps shall be two, type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 87, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

Where the bumper lighting performs the daytime running lamp function: the distance between the inner edges of the apparent surfaces of the daytime running lamps in the direction of the reference axes shall not be less than 600 mm; this distance may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.
Where the bumper lighting performs the daytime running lamp function: daytime running lamps shall be mounted not less than 250 mm nor more than 1,500 mm above the ground.

Where the bumper lighting performs the daytime running lamp function: daytime running lamps shall be located at the front of the vehicle; this is deemed satisfied if the light emitted does not cause discomfort to the driver either directly or indirectly through the devices for indirect vision and/or other reflecting surfaces of the vehicle.
Where the bumper lighting performs the daytime running lamp function: daytime running lamps shall have a horizontal geometric visibility of 20° outwards and 20° inwards.
Where the bumper lighting performs the daytime running lamp function: daytime running lamps shall have a vertical geometric visibility of 10° upwards and 10° downwards.
Where the bumper lighting performs the daytime running lamp function: daytime running lamps shall be oriented towards the front.

Where the bumper lighting performs the daytime running lamp function: the daytime running lamps shall be switched ON automatically when the device which starts and/or stops the propulsion system is set in a position which makes it possible for the propulsion system to operate and none of the following exist: (a) the front fog lamps are switched ON; (b) the headlamps are manually switched ON, except when used to give intermittent luminous warnings at short intervals; (c) conditions of Annex 13 for automatic switching ON of dipped-beam headlamps exist.

Where the bumper lighting performs the daytime running lamp function: irrespective of paragraphs 6.19.7.1. and 6.19.7.5., under conditions requiring the daytime running lamps to be switched ON, they may remain OFF or, once automatically switched ON, may be switched OFF manually and remain OFF while at least one of the following exists: (a) the automatic transmission control is in the park position; (b) the parking brake is in the locked position; (c) prior to the vehicle being set in motion for the first time after each manual activation of the device which starts and/or stops the propulsion system; (d) the vehicle speed does not exceed 15 km/h.

Where the bumper lighting performs the daytime running lamp function: automatic operation of the daytime running lamps shall be resumed as soon as the conditions described in paragraph 6.19.7.2. no longer exist.

Where the bumper lighting performs the daytime running lamp function: the daytime running lamp shall switch OFF automatically when the device which starts and/or stops the propulsion system is set in a position which makes it impossible for the propulsion system to operate, as well as when either of the following exists: (a) the front fog lamps are switched ON; (b) the headlamps are manually switched ON, except when used to give intermittent luminous warnings at short intervals; (c) conditions of Annex 13 for automatic switching ON of dipped-beam headlamps exist.

Where the bumper lighting performs the daytime running lamp function: when the daytime running lamps are switched ON, the rear position lamps shall be switched ON and any other lamp(s) mentioned in paragraph 5.11. may also be switched ON; however, the rear position lamps and the other lamp(s) may be switched OFF and remain OFF while the daytime running lamps are ON as long as the ambient light outside the vehicle is above 7,000 lux (measured according to Annex 13).

Where the bumper lighting performs the daytime running lamp function and a front direction-indicator lamp is not reciprocally incorporated with it and the distance between the edges of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of the front direction-indicator lamp and the daytime running lamp is 40 mm or less, the electrical connections of the daytime running lamp shall be such that either (a) the daytime running lamp on the relevant side is switched OFF during the entire period (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the front direction-indicator lamp, or (b) its luminous intensity is reduced during that entire period to not more than 140 cd within the angles of geometric visibility; switching OFF or dimming is not required if the luminous intensity of the front direction-indicator lamp in HV is at least 50% higher than that of the daytime running lamp in HV, in which case compliance shall be demonstrated with a concise description or other means acceptable to the Type Approval Authority.

Where the bumper lighting performs the daytime running lamp function and a front direction-indicator lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the daytime running lamp with totally common apparent surfaces, the electrical connections shall be such that the daytime running lamp function on the relevant side of the vehicle is switched OFF during the entire period (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the front direction-indicator lamp.

Where the bumper lighting performs the daytime running lamp function and a front direction-indicator lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the daytime running lamp with partially common apparent surfaces, the electrical connections of the daytime running lamp shall be such that either (a) the whole daytime running lamp function on the relevant side is switched OFF during the entire period (both ON and OFF cycle) of activation of the front direction-indicator lamp, or (b) for a category 1a or 1b front direction-indicator lamp, the daytime running lamp function on the relevant side is switched OFF for the part of the apparent surface in common with the front direction-indicator lamp and the luminous intensity of the part not in common is reduced during the entire period (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the front direction-indicator lamp to not more than 140 cd within the angles of geometric visibility.

Where the bumper lighting performs the daytime running lamp function: a closed-circuit tell-tale is optional; however, a tell-tale indicating failure is mandatory if required by the component regulation.

If cornering lamps are integrated in the bumper: the number shall be two, type-approved according to the 01 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 119, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 149.
If cornering lamps are integrated in the bumper: one cornering lamp shall be located on each side of the vehicle's median longitudinal plane.
If cornering lamps are integrated in the bumper: cornering lamps shall be located not further than 1,000 mm from the front.

If cornering lamps are integrated in the bumper: cornering lamps shall be mounted not less than 250 mm and not more than 900 mm above the ground; however, no point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis shall be higher than the highest point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the dipped-beam headlamp.
If cornering lamps are integrated in the bumper: geometric visibility defined by angles α and β (paragraph 2.10.7.) shall be α = 10° upwards and downwards and β = 30° to 60° outwards.
If cornering lamps are integrated in the bumper: cornering lamps shall be oriented such that they meet the requirements for geometric visibility.

If cornering lamps are integrated in the bumper: cornering lamps shall be so connected that they cannot be switched ON unless the main-beam headlamps or the dipped-beam headlamps are switched ON at the same time.

If cornering lamps are integrated in the bumper: the cornering lamp on one side of the vehicle may only be switched ON automatically when the direction-indicators on the same side are switched ON and/or when the steering angle is changed from the straight-ahead position towards the same side.

If cornering lamps are integrated in the bumper: the cornering lamp shall be switched OFF automatically when the direction-indicator is switched OFF and/or the steering angle has returned to the straight-ahead position.

If cornering lamps are integrated in the bumper: when the reversing lamp is switched ON, both cornering lamps may be switched ON simultaneously, independently of steering wheel position or direction-indicator operation.

If both cornering lamps are switched ON together with the reversing lamp, they shall be switched OFF either (a) when the reversing lamp is switched OFF, or (b) when the forward speed of the vehicle exceeds 15 km/h.
If cornering lamps are integrated in the bumper: no tell-tale is required; however, a tell-tale indicating failure is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
If cornering lamps are integrated in the bumper: the cornering lamps shall not be switched ON at vehicle speeds above 40 km/h.

If the bumper integrates an exterior courtesy lamp: the number of exterior courtesy lamps shall be one or two. Further exterior courtesy lamps to illuminate steps and/or door handles and/or the area around the vehicle are permitted.
If the bumper integrates an exterior courtesy lamp: each door handle or step shall be illuminated by not more than one lamp.

If the bumper integrates an exterior courtesy lamp: the exterior courtesy lamp(s) shall not be switched ON unless the vehicle is stationary and one or more of the following conditions is satisfied: (a) the propulsion system is stopped; or (b) a driver or passenger door is opened or after being closed; or (c) a load compartment door is opened or after being closed. However, the exterior courtesy lamp(s) shall be switched OFF when the vehicle is no longer stationary.
If the bumper integrates an exterior courtesy lamp: the exterior courtesy lamps may be switched ON and/or switched OFF manually or automatically.

If the bumper integrates an exterior courtesy lamp: the exterior courtesy lamp(s) may vary in luminous intensity and/or in apparent surface, and their photometric characteristics may vary in relation to the position of vehicle users; no sharp variation of intensity shall be observed during transition.
If the bumper integrates an exterior courtesy lamp: the exterior courtesy lamp(s) shall not flash.
If the bumper integrates an exterior courtesy lamp: at the discretion of the manufacturer the exterior courtesy lamp(s) may operate in any combination.

If the bumper lamps are used as exterior courtesy lamps: approved lamps emitting white light, with the exception of main-beam headlamps, daytime running lamps and reversing lamps, may be switched ON as exterior courtesy lamp(s); in addition, parking lamps, side-marker lamps and/or end-outline marker lamps may be switched ON; the conditions of paragraphs 5.11. and 5.12. may not apply.

If the bumper integrates an exterior courtesy lamp: there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of the exterior courtesy lamps when viewed by an observer moving on the boundary of a zone formed by a transverse plane 10 m from the front of the vehicle, a transverse plane 10 m from the rear and two longitudinal planes 10 m from each side of the vehicle, these planes extending from 1 m to 3 m above and perpendicular to the ground as shown in Annex 14. At the request of the applicant and with the consent of the Technical Service, this may be verified by drawing or simulation, or deemed satisfied if the luminous intensity of light emitted directly during the Annex 14 observation test is not more than 0.5 cd per lamp.

If the bumper integrates a side-mounted manoeuvring lamp: the number shall be one or two (one per side) on vehicles not exceeding 6 m in length, a maximum of four (up to two per side) on vehicles above 6 m and up to and including 9 m, and a maximum of six (up to three per side) on vehicles exceeding 9 m.

If the bumper integrates a manoeuvring lamp: the installed manoeuvring lamp shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 23, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
If the bumper integrates a side-mounted manoeuvring lamp: its height above the ground shall be not more than 1,500 mm.
If the bumper integrates side-mounted manoeuvring lamps and more than one manoeuvring lamp is installed: the lamps shall be mounted as symmetrically as practicable along each side of the vehicle.
If more than one side-mounted manoeuvring lamp is installed on the same side: the distance between two adjacent manoeuvring lamps on the same side shall not be less than 0.5 m.
If the bumper integrates a manoeuvring lamp: its orientation shall be downwards, subject to the requirements of paragraph 6.26.9.

If the bumper integrates a manoeuvring lamp (motor vehicle): the manoeuvring lamps shall be so connected that they cannot be switched ON unless the main-beam headlamps or the dipped-beam headlamps are switched ON at the same time.

If the bumper integrates a manoeuvring lamp (motor vehicle): the manoeuvring lamp(s) shall be switched ON automatically for slow manoeuvres up to 15 km/h provided that one of the following conditions is fulfilled: (a) prior to the vehicle being set in motion for the first time after each manual activation of the propulsion system; or (b) reverse gear is engaged; or (c) a camera-based system which assists parking manoeuvres is operating.

If the bumper integrates a manoeuvring lamp (motor vehicle): the manoeuvring lamps shall be automatically switched OFF if the forward speed of the vehicle exceeds 15 km/h and shall remain switched OFF until the switch ON conditions are met again.

If the bumper integrates a manoeuvring lamp: there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of the manoeuvring lamps when viewed by an observer moving on the boundary of a zone formed by a transverse plane 10 m from the front of the vehicle, a transverse plane 10 m from the rear and two longitudinal planes 10 m from each side of the vehicle, these planes extending from 1 m to 3 m above the ground as shown in Annex 14. At the request of the applicant and with the consent of the Technical Service, this may be verified by drawing or simulation, or deemed satisfied if the installation conditions comply with paragraph 6.2.2. of UN Regulation No. 23, paragraph 5.10.2. of the 00 series of UN Regulation No. 148 or paragraph 5.10.1.2. of the 01 and subsequent series of UN Regulation No. 148.

The position of each lamp in width, in height and in length, checked in accordance with paragraphs 2.10.2., 2.10.3., 2.10.4., 2.3.3. and 5.4. of the Regulation, shall be such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled.

The angles of geometric visibility of each lamp, checked in accordance with paragraph 2.10.7., shall be such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled, except that the limits of the angles may have an allowance corresponding to the ±3° variation permitted in paragraph 5.3. for the mounting of the light-signalling devices.
The lamps shall meet paragraph 5.10. of the Regulation with regard to the visibility of red light towards the front and of white light towards the rear.

When every lamp supplied by the electrical system of the vehicle is switched on, the lamps and tell-tales shall function in accordance with paragraphs 5.11. to 5.14. of the Regulation and with the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.

The presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, the category of the lamps, checked by visual inspection of the lamps and their markings, shall be such that the requirements of paragraphs 5.15. and 5.16. and the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled.

If a front fog lamp or dipped-beam headlamp is integrated in the bumper: the initial downward inclination of the cut-off of the dipped beam and of the front fog lamp shall be set to the plated figure as required and shown in Annex 7; alternatively, the manufacturer shall set the initial aim to a figure different from the plated figure where it can be shown to be representative of the type approved when tested in accordance with Annex 6, in particular paragraph 4.1.

If a dipped-beam headlamp is integrated in the bumper: the variation of the dipped-beam downward inclination as a function of the loading conditions shall remain within the range given in the table of Annex 9 paragraph 1.3.2., with the loading states of Annex 5 applied for every system adjusted accordingly; for category M1 vehicles the loading states are Annex 5 paragraphs 2.1.1.1. and 2.1.1.6., taking into account paragraph 2.1.2.

If a dipped-beam headlamp is integrated in the bumper: dipped-beam downward inclination variation limits by mounting height h: for 0.5 m ≤ h ≤ 0.9 m, upper limit -0.50 per cent and lower limit -(h + 1.2) per cent; for 0.9 m < h ≤ 1.2 m, upper limit -(h x 2.17 - 1.45) per cent and lower limit -(h x 2.17 + 0.15) per cent.

If a front fog lamp with light source(s) having a total objective luminous flux exceeding 2,000 lumens is integrated in the bumper: the variation of its downward inclination as a function of the loading conditions shall remain within 0.7 per cent minimum and 3.3 per cent maximum vertical inclination for h < 0.8 m, and within 1.2 per cent minimum and 3.8 per cent maximum vertical inclination for h > 0.8 m.

If a dipped-beam headlamp is integrated in the bumper of the M1 vehicle: the angle of the light beam of the dipped-beam headlamps shall be determined under the load conditions of Annex 5 paragraphs 2.1.1.1. to 2.1.1.6. (passenger mass 75 kg per person), taking account of any loading restrictions laid down by the manufacturer.

If a dipped-beam headlamp is integrated in the bumper: the variations in dipped-beam or vehicle inclination, measured separately for each side of the vehicle, shall for both left and right headlamps under all load conditions of Annex 5 be within the limits set out in Annex 6 paragraph 5.5.

If a dipped-beam headlamp is integrated in the bumper: requirements are met on a single measurement per loading condition if, for all loading conditions, the variation in inclination is within the calculated limits (difference between the stated initial inclination and the lower and upper limits specified for approval) with a safety margin of 4 mrad (0.4 per cent inclination).

If a dipped-beam headlamp is integrated in the bumper: requirements are met if, under all loading conditions, the variation between the measured initial inclination determined according to Annex 6 paragraph 5.2. and the inclination measured under each loading condition is less than the values calculated in paragraph 5.5.1. (without safety margin).

If a dipped-beam headlamp is integrated in the bumper and only one of the calculated upper or lower limits of variation is exceeded, the manufacturer is permitted to choose a different value for the stated initial inclination, within the limits specified for approval.

If a main-beam headlamp is integrated in the bumper: the aggregate maximum intensity of the main-beam headlamps, checked by the procedure of paragraph 6.1.9.2., shall fulfil the requirement of paragraph 6.1.9.1.

If the camera is used as sensor for automatic dipped-beam switching: with ambient light outside the vehicle less than 1,000 lux, the dipped-beam headlamps shall be switched ON with a response time of no more than 2 seconds.

If the camera is used as sensor for automatic dipped-beam switching: with ambient light outside the vehicle more than 7,000 lux, the dipped-beam headlamps shall be switched OFF with a response time of more than 5 seconds but no more than 300 seconds.

If the camera is used as sensor for automatic dipped-beam switching: with ambient light outside the vehicle between 1,000 lux and 7,000 lux, the dipped-beam headlamp state and response time are at the manufacturer's discretion.

If the camera is used as sensor for automatic dipped-beam switching: the ambient illuminance for the switching conditions shall be measured on a horizontal surface with a cosine-corrected sensor at the same height as the mounting position of the sensor on the vehicle.

A separate approval under UN R148 is required for each lamp (function) listed in paragraph 1 that the side signalling lamp performs (e.g. side marker lamp, direction indicator, position lamp, parking lamp, daytime running lamp).

If the side signalling lamp is part of a unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, each of these lamps shall satisfy the provisions of this Regulation or of another Regulation, and lamps not satisfying the provisions of any of those Regulations shall not be part of such unit.
The lamp shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and the other markings defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
All markings on the lamp shall be clearly legible and indelible.
With regard to the size of the approval marking, the value for "a" shall be at least 5 mm.
The lamp shall bear the approval marking.

The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.

The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the light-signalling lamp function(s) for which approval has been granted, as prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4. (Table 1).

If the lamp is approved as a side marker lamp for M1 vehicles, the identifying symbol shall be "SM2" (paragraph 5.7.).

If the lamp is a direction indicator of category 6, an indication "R" or "L" shall be shown on the lamp, indicating the right or left side of the vehicle.
If the lamp may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps, the additional letter "D" shall be marked to the right side of the function symbol.
If the lamp is used as part of an interdependent lamp system, the additional letter "Y" shall be marked to the right side of the function symbol.
The lamp shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.

If replaceable light source module(s) are used, each light source module shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.

If replaceable light source module(s) are used, each light source module shall bear the specific identification code of the module, comprising the starting letters "MD" followed by the approval mark without the circle as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.2.1.1.; the approval mark need not be the same as the one on the lamp but both marks shall be from the same applicant.
If several non-identical light source modules are used, the specific identification code of each module shall be followed by additional symbols or characters.
If replaceable light source module(s) are used, each light source module shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
If replaceable light source module(s) are used, the lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.3.5. (a)(ii).
If replaceable light source module(s) are used, the lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
An electronic light source control gear being part of the lamp but not included in the lamp body shall be marked with its identification number.
An electronic light source control gear being part of the lamp but not included in the lamp body shall be marked with the name of the manufacturer.
The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp which is not designed to be separated from the transparent part of the lamp emitting the light.

The approval marking, as well as the category or categories of LED substitute light source(s) prescribed, if any, shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood, boot lid or a door is opened.

The markings of paragraphs 3.3.3.2., 3.3.3.3. (a), 3.3.3.4., 3.3.3.5. and 3.3.3.6. (trade name, light source categories, rated voltage, module markings, control gear markings) do not need to be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle.
If an outer lens is used for several devices bearing different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
The approval marking and the markings of paragraphs 3.3.3.2., 3.3.3.3., 3.3.3.4., 3.3.3.5. (b) and 3.3.3.6. shall be affixed on the lamp.
If replaceable light source module(s) are used, the markings of paragraph 3.3.3.5. (a) shall be affixed on the light source module.

Where grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps have been found to comply with the requirements of several UN Regulations, a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number may be affixed, located anywhere on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, provided the conditions of paragraphs 3.3.5.1.1. and 3.3.5.1.2. are met.
If a single approval mark is used for grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, it shall be visible after their installation.

If a single approval mark is used for grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of these lamps that transmits light shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark.

If a single approval mark is used for grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, the size of its components shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.

The requirements of sections 5 'General specifications' and 6 'Individual specifications' (and the Annexes referenced in them) of UN Regulation No. 48, in the series of amendments in force at the time of application for lamp type approval, shall apply to the lamp. The requirements pertinent to the lamp's function and to vehicle category M1 apply where their verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.

The lamp shall be designed and constructed so that, in normal conditions of use and notwithstanding the vibrations it may be subjected to, its satisfactory operation remains assured and it retains the characteristics prescribed by UN R148.

If the lamp is an assembly of two independent lamps to be type approved as a lamp marked 'D', this arrangement is applicable only to front position lamps, end-outline marker lamps, daytime running lamps and direction indicator lamps (not to side marker lamps or parking lamps).

If the lamp is part of an interdependent lamp system to be type approved as lamps marked 'Y', this arrangement is applicable only to front position lamps, end-outline marker lamps, daytime running lamps and direction indicator lamps (not to side marker lamps or parking lamps).
If the lamp is approved as a front position lamp, it is deemed also to be approved as a front end-outline marker lamp.
If the lamp is a front position lamp that is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with another function, it may also be used as an end-outline marker lamp.

If the lamp incorporates a manufacturer logo: on request of the applicant, the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside the apparent surface of the lamp (function) may incorporate only one manufacturer logo, made of transparent or non-transparent components. If the lamp incorporates a logo: irrespective of the marking requirements of paragraph 3.3., only the logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or the body manufacturer shall be allowed, as confirmed by an applicant statement (paragraph 3.1.2.2. (f)).

If the lamp incorporates a logo: the enclosed light emitting surface of the logo (incorporating its transparent and non-transparent components) in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 100 cm2.

If the lamp incorporates a logo: notwithstanding paragraph 5.5.2. of UN Regulation No. 48, the logo light emitting surface (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components) does not have to be symmetrical by itself.
If the lamp provides a direction indicator function, it shall not incorporate a logo.

In a single lamp containing more than one light source, a group of light sources wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light shall be considered to be one light source.

For a single lamp containing more than one light source that is a side marker lamp, front position lamp, parking lamp or side direction indicator of category 5 or 6: in case of failure of any one light source, at least one of the following provisions shall apply. (a) The light intensity complies with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution in Annex 3, and the maximum intensities are not exceeded when all light sources are illuminated. (b) A signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraphs 6.4.8., 6.7.8., 6.9.8., 6.10.8., 6.11.8., 6.12.8., 6.13.8. and 6.18.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, is produced; in this case the lamp is only for use on a vehicle fitted with a failure tell-tale (noted in the communication form).

If the lamp is a daytime running lamp containing more than one light source, instead of paragraph 4.6.1.2. (and in addition to paragraph 4.6.1.1.): in case of failure of any one light source, at least one of the following shall apply. (a) The light intensity at the points of standard light distribution defined in paragraph 2.2. of Annex 3 is at least 80 per cent of the minimum intensity required. (b) A signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraph 6.19.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, is produced; in this case the lamp is only for use on a vehicle fitted with a failure tell-tale (noted in the communication form).

If the lamp is a front direction indicator of category 1, 1a or 1b, instead of paragraph 4.6.1.2. (and in addition to paragraph 4.6.1.1.), a signal for activation of the tell-tale prescribed in paragraph 6.5.8. of UN Regulation No. 48 shall be produced on the basis of one of the following options. (a) Any one light source has failed. (b) For a lamp designed for only two light sources, the intensity in the axis of reference is less than 50 per cent of the minimum intensity required. (c) As a consequence of a failure of one or more light sources, the intensity in one of the following directions (paragraph 2.1. of Annex 3) is less than the minimum intensity required: H=0°, V=0°; H=20° outwards, V=+5°; H=10° inwards, V=0°.

The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light source(s) approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128 (provided that no restriction on their use is made at the time of application for type approval), and/or light source module(s), and/or non-replaceable light source(s).
If the lamp uses replaceable UN approved light source(s), the design of the lamp shall be such that the light source(s) can be fixed in no other position but the correct one.

If the lamp uses replaceable UN approved light source(s), the light source holder shall conform to the characteristics given in IEC Publication 60061, using the holder data sheet relevant to the prescribed light source category.

If the lamp uses replaceable UN approved light source(s) and a category of LED substitute light source is also prescribed, the light source holder shall also conform to the IEC 60061 holder data sheet relevant to the category of LED substitute light source.
The light-signalling device shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances that cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.
If the lamp uses replaceable light source module(s), the light source module shall be designed so that it can only be fitted in the designated and correct position.
If the lamp uses replaceable light source module(s), the light source module shall be designed so that it can only be removed with the use of tool(s).
If the lamp uses replaceable light source module(s), the light source module shall be tamperproof.

If the lamp uses replaceable light source module(s), the light source module shall, regardless of the use of tool(s), not be interchangeable with any replaceable UN approved light source and/or with any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics located in the same lamp housing.

If the lamp uses replaceable light source module(s): when the light source module is removed and replaced by another module provided by the applicant bearing the same light source module identification code, the lamp shall still meet the photometric requirements.
If the lamp uses replaceable UN approved light sources, all photometric and colorimetric measurements shall be made using standard light sources as specified in R.E.5.
If the lamp is equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), all photometric and colorimetric measurements shall be made with the light source(s) present in the lamp.

If the lamp, at the discretion of the applicant, is also to be approved with LED substitute light source(s), all photometric and colorimetric measurements shall be repeated using the prescribed LED substitute light source(s).
If not otherwise specified, the luminous intensities of the lamp shall be measured with the light source continuously lit.

Where measurement results are challenged, the intensity requirement for a particular direction of observation shall be deemed satisfied if it is met in a direction deviating by not more than one-quarter of a degree from the direction of observation.
Unless otherwise specified, the lamp shall be tested with a supply voltage at the lamp of 6.75 V (6 V systems), 13.5 V (12 V systems) or 28 V (24 V systems).
If the lamp is controlled by an electronic light source control gear, the lamp shall be operated for testing as specified by the applicant.

If the lamp is not controlled by an electronic light source control gear and uses light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), the lamp shall be operated for testing as specified by the applicant.

If the lamp is not controlled by an electronic light source control gear and uses replaceable UN approved light source(s), the light sources shall be operated for testing at the reference/objective luminous flux, or alternatively at a different luminous flux with a proportional correction on the measured luminous intensities.

If not otherwise specified, the luminous intensity emitted by each of the two samples on the reference axis (HV) shall be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

If not otherwise specified, the luminous intensity emitted by each of the two samples shall, in no direction where the lamp is visible, exceed the maximum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

If not otherwise specified, the luminous intensity emitted by each of the two samples outside the reference axis shall be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5. multiplied by the percentage given in the pertinent light distribution figure of Annex 3 for each direction, or not less than the intensity value specified in that figure for each direction.

If not otherwise specified, the luminous intensity emitted by each of the two samples within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2 shall be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
The luminous intensity of the lamp shall observe the provisions of the relevant paragraphs of Annex 3 on local variations of intensity.

If the lamp is an assembly of two independent lamps type approved as lamps marked 'D' with the same function and deemed to be a single lamp, it shall comply with the maximum intensity requirements when all lamps are lit together.

If the lamp is an assembly of two independent lamps type approved as lamps marked 'D' with the same function and deemed to be a single lamp, it shall comply with the minimum intensity requirements if either lamp has failed.
If the lamp is part of an interdependent lamp system (marked 'Y'), the system shall meet the requirements when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
Tests for compliance of the luminous intensities of the lamp shall be carried out according to Annex 8.

The colour of the light emitted by the lamp shall be measured inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in the relevant paragraph of Annex 3, applying the test procedure of paragraph 4.8.
Outside the field of the light distribution grid of Annex 3 for the function, no sharp variation of the colour of the light emitted by the lamp shall be observed.

If the lamp is a front position lamp (A) or front end-outline marker lamp (AM), the colour of the light emitted shall be white.
If the side signalling lamp is a (front) parking lamp (77R), the light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 5.
