For a lamp equipped with a replaceable light source, the heat resistance test shall use a light source of the category specified for the lamp, supplied at a voltage giving the specified average power at the corresponding test voltage, or, where only the maximum power is specified, at a voltage giving 90 per cent of the specified power; the specified average or maximum power shall be chosen from the rated voltage(s) of 6, 12 or 24 V at which it reaches the highest value.
After the heat resistance test and stabilization at ambient temperature, no distortion, deformation, cracking or colour modification of the lamp shall be perceptible.

In case of doubt after the heat resistance test, the luminous intensity measured according to paragraph 5. of this Regulation shall reach at least 90 per cent of the values obtained before the heat resistance test on the same lamp.

If the lamp (function) uses incandescent technology only (replaceable filament light source option), the luminous intensities measured after photometric stability shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

For a lamp (function) using light source technologies other than incandescent only (e.g. LED), the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements; the distribution after 1 minute may be calculated from the distribution after 30 minutes or after photometric stabilization by applying at each test point the ratio of the intensities measured at HV.

If the lamp is a direction indicator lamp using non-incandescent technology, it shall be operated in flashing mode (f = 1.5 Hz, duty factor 50 per cent) for the luminous intensity measurements after 1 minute and after 30 minutes or photometric stability.

Depending on the light source technology, the luminous intensity distribution of the lamp (function) shall in addition be compliant at the point in time after switch ON listed in Table A8-1; it may be calculated from the distribution measured according to paragraph 1 by applying at each test point the ratio of luminous intensities measured at the reference coordinate of the lamp (function).
If the lamp is a direction indicator of category 1 (incl. 1a, 1b), its luminous intensity distribution shall be compliant 0.2 s after switch ON, with HV as reference coordinate.
If the lamp is a direction indicator of category 5 or 6, its luminous intensity distribution shall be compliant 0.2 s after switch ON, with H5, V0 as reference coordinate.
If the lamp acts as a front position lamp, its luminous intensity distribution shall be compliant 4 s after switch ON, with HV as reference coordinate.
If the lamp is an end-outline marker lamp, its luminous intensity distribution shall be compliant 4 s after switch ON, with HV as reference coordinate.
If the lamp is a parking lamp, its luminous intensity distribution shall be compliant 4 s after switch ON, with HV as reference coordinate.
If the lamp acts as a daytime running lamp, its luminous intensity distribution shall be compliant 4 s after switch ON, with HV as reference coordinate.
If the lamp is a side marker lamp, its luminous intensity distribution shall be compliant 4 s after switch ON, with HV as reference coordinate.

If the lamp (function) uses incandescent technology only, it is deemed to comply with the intensity requirements at all points in time if the values measured according to Annex 8 paragraph 1.1. are compliant.
If the lamp (function) uses LED technology only, it is deemed to comply with the intensity requirements at all points in time if the values measured according to Annex 8 paragraph 1.2. are compliant.

In case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour), the lamp (function) shall comply with the minimum intensity requirements at all points in time starting at the point in time listed in Table A8-1 and ending when photometric stability is reached.

After each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in Annex 3, the lighting and signalling devices (including the side signalling lamp integrated in the front bumper, and the decorative lighting if fitted) shall continue to operate correctly.

After each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in Annex 3, the lighting and signalling devices (including the side signalling lamp integrated in the front bumper, and the decorative lighting if fitted) shall remain visible.
After each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in Annex 3, the vehicle's bonnet (hood) shall be operable in the normal manner.

After each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in Annex 3, the vehicle's cooling system (behind the grille and bumper) shall have neither leaks nor constricted fluid passages which prevent normal functioning.
After each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in Annex 3, the sealing devices and caps of the vehicle's cooling system shall be operable in the normal manner.

After each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in Annex 3, the vehicle's propulsion, suspension (including tyres), steering and braking systems shall remain in adjustment and shall operate in a normal manner (where the EV charging inlet/flap is present in the bumper, this includes the propulsion/energy-supply parts in the impact zone); this requirement does not apply to sensors, cameras, radar devices, etc. being part of driver assist systems (e.g. the bumper's camera, radar, radar/LIDAR and PDC sensors), which may become damaged, disoriented or broken due to an impact carried out according to Annex 3 as long as the basic braking and steering performance are still intact.

Every vehicle bearing an approval mark under this Regulation shall conform to the vehicle type approved, particularly as regards features which influence the behaviour of the parts of the structure and the components affected by impact (e.g. the front protective device's dimensions, lines and materials).

In the impact tests of Annex 3, the first contact of the impactor with the vehicle shall be by the impact contour on the front protective device (bumper), the impactor reference line being at the reference height of 445 mm.

In both vehicle-loading conditions (unladen weight and laden test weight), the front protective device between the vehicle corners (as defined in paragraph 3.1.5.) shall be intersected by the horizontal plane passing through the impactor reference line at the reference height of 445 mm.
The effective mass of the impactor used to test the front protective device shall be equal to the mass corresponding to the unladen weight of the vehicle tested.

The front protective device shall be subjected to a longitudinal impact test consisting of two impacts on the front surface of the vehicle: one with the vehicle at unladen weight (paragraph 3.1.3.) and one with the vehicle at laden test weight (paragraph 3.1.4.).

For the two longitudinal impacts on the front surface, the location of the first impact is free, but for the second impact the median plane of the impactor shall be at least 300 mm from the first, provided that the extremities of the impactor do not pass outside the zone defined by two planes parallel to the longitudinal median plane passing through the vehicle corners.

In the front longitudinal impact test, the impactor is placed with plane A vertical and the reference line horizontal at 445 mm, and the vehicle is aligned so that a point between the vehicle corners touches the impactor with the vehicle's longitudinal median plane perpendicular to plane A.
In the front longitudinal impact test, the vehicle is impacted at a speed of 4 km/h +0.25/-0 km/h.

The front protective device shall be subjected to a corner impact test consisting of an impact at one front corner with the vehicle at unladen weight (paragraph 3.1.3.) and an impact at the other front corner with the vehicle at the weight given in paragraph 3.1.4. (laden test weight).

In the front corner impact test, with plane A of the impactor vertical and the reference line horizontal at 445 mm and a vehicle corner touching the impactor, plane A of the impactor shall make an angle of 60 ± 5° with the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle.
In the front corner impact test, the point of first contact on the vehicle shall be in the vertical median plane of the impactor within a tolerance of ± 25 mm.
In the front corner impact test, the vehicle is impacted at a speed of 2.5 km/h +0.1/-0 km/h.
The front protective device and the mountings attaching it to the vehicle structure may be repaired or replaced between the impact tests.
If the front protective device includes self-restoring materials (e.g. a recoverable EPP absorber), the permitted recovery time between tests shall be as stated by the manufacturer.
If the manufacturer so requests, a vehicle of the same type may be used for each impact test.

If the impact test has been carried out at an impact speed or with an impact mass exceeding those indicated in paragraphs 2.7.5. and 2.8.4. of Annex 3, and the vehicle has satisfied the prescribed conditions, the test is considered satisfactory.

Other equivalent test methods are permitted for verifying the front protective device, provided that the conditions referred to in this Regulation can be observed and their equivalence can be demonstrated.

Where the bumper's radar/LIDAR/camera sensors feed the vehicle's AEBS: the AEBS, when activated and operated within the prescribed speed ranges, shall meet the performance requirements of paragraphs 5.1. and 5.3. to 5.6. of UN R152 (all vehicles).

Where the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS and the vehicle is submitted to approval for the car to car scenario: the AEBS, when activated and operated within the prescribed speed ranges, shall meet the performance requirements of paragraph 5.2.1.

Where the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS and the vehicle is submitted to approval for the car to pedestrian scenario: the AEBS, when activated and operated within the prescribed speed ranges, shall meet the performance requirements of paragraph 5.2.2.

Where the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS and the vehicle is submitted to approval for the car to bicycle scenario: the AEBS, when activated and operated within the prescribed speed ranges, shall meet the performance requirements of paragraph 5.2.3.

Where the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS: the effectiveness of the AEBS shall not be adversely affected by magnetic or electrical fields, demonstrated by fulfilling the technical requirements and respecting the transitional provisions of the 06 series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 10.
Where the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS: conformity with the safety aspects of electronic control systems shall be shown by meeting the requirements of Annex 3 of UN R152.

Where the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS: the system shall provide the driver with a failure warning when there is a failure in the AEBS that prevents the requirements of UN R152 from being met; the warning shall be as specified in paragraph 5.5.4.
Where the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS: there shall not be an appreciable time interval between each AEBS self-check.

Where the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS: in the case of an electrically detectable failure (e.g. sensor or sensor heater fault), there shall not be a delay in illuminating the failure warning signal after the self-check.

Where the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS: upon detection of any non-electrical failure condition (e.g. sensor blindness or sensor misalignment), the failure warning signal defined in paragraph 5.1.4.1. shall be illuminated.

Where the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS: if the system has not been initialised after a cumulative driving time of 15 seconds above a speed of 10 km/h, information of this status shall be indicated to the driver.
Where the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS: the information that the system has not been initialised shall exist until the system has been successfully initialised.

Where the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS: subject to paragraphs 5.3.1. and 5.3.2., the system shall provide the emergency braking interventions described in paragraphs 5.2.1.2., 5.2.2.2. and 5.2.3.2. having the purpose of significantly decreasing the speed of the subject vehicle.

Where the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS: the system shall be designed to minimise the generation of collision warning signals in situations where there is no risk of an imminent collision, demonstrated in the Annex 3 assessment including in particular the scenarios listed in Appendix 2 of Annex 3.

Where the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS: the system shall be designed to avoid advanced emergency braking in situations where there is no risk of an imminent collision, demonstrated in the Annex 3 assessment including in particular the scenarios listed in Appendix 2 of Annex 3.

Car to car scenario (sensors feed the AEBS): when an imminent collision with a preceding M1 vehicle in the same lane is detected with a relative speed above that up to which the subject vehicle can avoid the collision (within the conditions of 5.2.1.4.), a collision warning shall be provided as specified in 5.5.1. and triggered at the latest 0.8 s before the start of emergency braking; however, where the collision cannot be anticipated in time to warn 0.8 s ahead, the warning shall be provided no later than the start of the emergency braking intervention; tested according to paragraphs 6.4. and 6.5.
Car to car scenario (sensors feed the AEBS): the collision warning may be aborted if the conditions prevailing a collision are no longer present.

Car to car scenario (sensors feed the AEBS): when the system has detected the possibility of an imminent collision, there shall be a braking demand of at least 5.0 m/s² to the service braking system; higher deceleration demands than 5 m/s² are not prohibited during the collision warning for very short durations (e.g. haptic warning), and the emergency braking may be aborted or the demand reduced below 5.0 m/s² if the conditions prevailing a collision are no longer present or the risk has decreased; tested in accordance with paragraphs 6.4. and 6.5.

Car to car scenario (sensors feed the AEBS): the system shall be active at least within the vehicle speed range between 10 km/h and 60 km/h and at all vehicle load conditions, unless deactivated as per paragraph 5.4.
