Where the bumper-integrated sensors feed the AEBS, upon a simulated electrical failure of any AEBS component (e.g. disconnection of the power source to the radar/LIDAR/camera or of any electrical connection between AEBS components, including the bumper harness), the failure warning signal of paragraph 5.5.4. shall be activated and remain activated not later than 10 s after the vehicle has been driven at a speed greater than 10 km/h, and be reactivated immediately after a subsequent ignition off/on cycle with the vehicle stationary as long as the failure exists.

Where the bumper-integrated sensors feed the AEBS, each test scenario (one setup, one subject vehicle speed, one load condition, one category) shall be passed by meeting the required performance in two test runs, with one repeat permitted if one of the two runs fails.
Where the bumper-integrated sensors feed the AEBS, the number of failed test runs for the Car to Car tests shall not exceed 10.0 per cent of the performed test runs.
Where the AEBS supports the car-to-pedestrian scenario, the number of failed test runs for the Car to Pedestrian tests shall not exceed 10.0 per cent of the performed test runs.
Where the AEBS supports the car-to-bicycle scenario, the number of failed test runs for the Car to Bicycle tests shall not exceed 20.0 per cent of the performed test runs.

During the assessment as per Annex 3, the manufacturer shall demonstrate via appropriate documentation that the AEBS (including the bumper-integrated sensors) is capable of reliably delivering the required performances.

At the manufacturer's request, virtual testing (e.g. using sensor models) may be used as an alternative for some of the tests of paragraphs 6.4. to 6.7.; the virtual testing shall be verified and validated according to Annex 4 and used in accordance with that Annex.

Where virtual testing is used, at least 30 per cent of the required tests shall be performed physically, including at least one test of each scenario variant of paragraphs 6.4 to 6.7 relevant for the approval.

Notwithstanding paragraph 6.11.3, in case of modification of the vehicle type and extension of approval, the proportion of physical tests may be less than 30 per cent of the required tests, as agreed between the manufacturer and the Type Approval Authority or its Technical Service.
Where virtual testing is used, a separate report including at least the additional information specified in Annex 4 shall be annexed to the test report.
A vehicle approved pursuant to R152 shall be so manufactured, including its AEBS sensors in the bumper module, as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements of paragraph 5.

If the bumper's radar, radar/LIDAR or camera feed the AEBS (forming part of "The System"), "The System" shall respect, under non-fault and fault conditions, all the appropriate performance requirements specified in UN R152, and the documentation disclosed to the Technical Service shall show this.
If the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS, "The System" shall be designed to operate in such a way that it does not induce safety critical risks.
If the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS, the documentation package shall describe how the current operational status of "The System" can be checked at periodic technical inspections.
If the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS, a list of all input and sensed variables of "The System" shall be provided and their working range defined.
If the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS, limits defining the boundaries of functional operation of "The System" shall be stated where appropriate to system performance.

If the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS, a list collating all units of "The System" (e.g. radar, radar/LIDAR, camera, harness links) shall be provided, together with an outline schematic showing the units in combination with equipment distribution and interconnections made clear.
If the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS, the function of each unit of "The System" shall be outlined and the signals linking it with other units or other vehicle systems shall be shown.

If the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS, interconnections within "The System" shall be shown by a circuit diagram for the electric transmission links, and the transmission links to and from other systems shall also be shown.

If the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS, there shall be a clear correspondence between the transmission links and the signals/operating data carried between units, and priorities of signals on multiplexed data paths shall be stated wherever priority may affect performance or safety.

If the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS, each unit of "The System" shall be clearly and unambiguously identifiable (e.g. by marking for hardware and marking or software output for software content) to provide corresponding hardware and documentation association.

If the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS, where functions are combined within a single unit or single computer but shown in multiple blocks in the block diagram, only a single hardware identification marking shall be used.

If the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS, the unit identification shall define the hardware and software version, and shall be changed where a software change alters the function of the unit as far as UN R152 is concerned.

If the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS, the strategy chosen to achieve "The System" objectives shall not, under non-fault conditions, prejudice the safe operation of the vehicle (manufacturer's statement required).

If the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS, for software employed in "The System" the outline architecture shall be explained, the design methods and tools identified, and evidence shown of how the system logic was realised during design and development.

If the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS, "The System" shall have design provisions generating safe operation under fault conditions (e.g. fall-back to partial system, change-over to back-up, or removal of the high level function), explained to the Technical Service.
If the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS, in case of a failure of "The System" (e.g. sensor or heater fault) the driver shall be warned, for example by warning signal or message display.

If the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS, the failure warning shall be present as long as the fault condition persists, unless the system is deactivated by the driver (e.g. ignition switched off or the function switched off via a dedicated switch).

If the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS and the chosen fault provision selects a partial performance mode under certain fault conditions, these conditions shall be stated and the resulting limits of effectiveness defined.

If the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS and the chosen fault provision selects a back-up means, the change-over principles, logic and level of redundancy and built-in back-up checking features shall be explained and the limits of back-up effectiveness defined.

If the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS and the chosen fault provision selects removal of the Higher Level Function, all corresponding output control signals associated with this function shall be inhibited in such a manner as to limit the transition disturbance.

If the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS, the documentation shall be supported by an analysis showing how the system behaves on the occurrence of any individual hazard or fault bearing on vehicle control performance or safety, based on a Hazard/Risk analysis at vehicle level (including interactions with other vehicle systems) and an FMEA, FTA or similar process at system level, with validation plans and results (e.g. HIL testing, on-road testing).

If the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS, the documentation shall itemize the parameters being monitored and set out, for each fault condition, the warning signal given to the driver and/or to service/technical inspection personnel.

If the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS, measures shall be in place, and documented, to ensure "The System" does not prejudice the safe operation of the vehicle when its performance is affected by environmental conditions, e.g. climatic, temperature, dust ingress, water ingress, ice packing.

If the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS, the reaction of "The System" to a simulated failure in any individual unit shall correspond with the documented summary of the failure analysis, to a level of overall effect such that the safety concept and execution are confirmed as adequate.

If the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS, the system shall implement strategies to minimize the generation of false reactions, and the vehicle manufacturer shall explain the principle strategies for each scenario type: (1) left/right turn at an intersection passing an oncoming stopped vehicle, (2) forward vehicle turning right/left while the subject vehicle goes straight, (3) curved road (radius ≤ 25 m) with guard pipes and a stationary vehicle, pedestrian or bicycle target outside the guard pipes, (4) lane change in front of a road-construction signboard.

If the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS, evidence (e.g. simulation results, real-world test data, track test data) of the system's behaviour (no false reaction) in each of the false-reaction scenarios 1 to 4 of Annex 3 Appendix 2 shall be provided, with the scenario parameters (speeds, TTC values, overlap/offset ratios) used as guidance if a demonstration is deemed necessary.

If the bumper's sensors feed the AEBS, compliance of the AEBS with the performance requirements of paragraphs 5.2.1 to 5.2.3 may be demonstrated by virtual testing of the dynamic manoeuvres of paragraphs 6.4 to 6.7, using a toolchain developed, verified and validated according to Annex 4.
If virtual testing is used for the AEBS, the toolchain (including sensor models of the bumper-mounted radar/LIDAR/camera) shall reflect the vehicle, system and components that are to be tested.
If virtual testing is used for the AEBS, the toolchain and its components shall be capable of accurately representing the relevant aspects of the physical AEBS that is being modelled.
For a vehicle with a lower bumper height of less than 425 mm, the front bumper shall meet the lower legform to bumper requirements of paragraph 4.1.1.

For a vehicle with a lower bumper height greater than or equal to 425 mm and less than 500 mm, the front bumper shall meet either the lower legform requirements of paragraph 4.1.1. or the upper legform requirements of paragraph 4.1.2., at the choice of the manufacturer.
For a vehicle with a lower bumper height greater than or equal to 500 mm, the front bumper shall meet the upper legform to bumper requirements of paragraph 4.1.2.

Where the lower legform test applies, compliance of the bumper with the performance requirements of paragraph 5.1.1. shall be verified using the flexible lower legform impactor specified in paragraph 6.3.1.1. and the test procedures specified in paragraph 7.1.1.

Where the upper legform test applies, compliance of the bumper with the performance requirements of paragraph 5.1.2. shall be verified using the upper legform impactor specified in paragraph 6.3.1.2. and the test procedures specified in paragraph 7.1.2.

Where the upper grille/fascia lies within the child headform test area (WAD1000 or more), compliance with the performance requirements of paragraph 5.2.1. shall be verified using the child headform impactor specified in paragraph 6.3.2.1. and the test procedures specified in paragraphs 7.2. and 7.3.

When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.1. (flexible lower legform to bumper), the absolute value of the maximum dynamic medial collateral ligament (MCL) elongation at the knee shall not exceed 22 mm.

When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.1. (flexible lower legform to bumper), the maximum dynamic anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) and posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) elongation shall not exceed 13 mm.

When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.1. (flexible lower legform to bumper), the absolute value of the dynamic bending moments at the tibia shall not exceed 340 Nm; however, the manufacturer may nominate bumper test widths up to a maximum of 264 mm in total where the absolute value of the tibia bending moment shall not exceed 380 Nm (a Contracting Party may restrict application of this relaxation zone).
When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.2. (upper legform to bumper), the instantaneous sum of the impact forces with respect to time shall not exceed 7.5 kN.
When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.2. (upper legform to bumper), the bending moment on the test impactor shall not exceed 510 Nm.

Where the pedestrian impact sensors form part of a Deployable Pedestrian Protection System (DPPS) and the vehicle is tested as a DPPS, the test conditions and requirements of Annex 1 shall apply to the headform tests.

Where the upper grille/fascia lies within the headform test area, when tested with the child headform in accordance with paragraphs 7.2., 7.3. and, if applicable (DPPS), Annex 1, the HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over a minimum of one half of the child headform test area and 1,000 over two thirds of the combined child and adult headform test areas, and the HIC for the remaining areas shall not exceed 1,700 for both headforms.
In case there is only a child headform test area, the HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over two thirds of the test area and shall not exceed 1,700 for the remaining area.
At the time of testing, the vehicle or sub-system (including the bumper) shall have a relative humidity of 40 % ± 30 % and a stabilized temperature of 20 ± 4 °C.

Where a complete vehicle is used for the test, it shall be in its normal ride attitude and either securely mounted on raised supports or at rest on a flat horizontal surface with the parking brake applied.

Where a cut-body is used for the test, it shall include all parts of the vehicle front structure (including the complete bumper module with its attachments), all under-bonnet components and all components behind the windscreen that may be involved in a frontal impact with a vulnerable road user.
Where a cut-body is used for the test, it shall be securely mounted in the normal vehicle ride attitude.

Where the pedestrian impact sensors are part of a device designed to protect vulnerable road users (DPPS), the device shall be correctly activated before and/or be active during the relevant test, and the manufacturer shall show that the device will act as intended in a pedestrian impact.

For bumper components which could change shape or position (other than active pedestrian protection devices) and which have more than one fixed shape or position (e.g. the optional EV charge flap), the vehicle shall comply with the components in each fixed shape or position.
When tested as a DPPS, the vehicle shall be adjusted as specified in the test procedure defined in Annex 1.
In the flexible lower legform to bumper test, the selected target points shall be in the bumper test area.

In the flexible lower legform to bumper test, the direction of the impact velocity vector shall be in the horizontal plane and parallel to the longitudinal vertical plane of the vehicle (tolerance ± 2° at first contact), with the impactor axis perpendicular to the horizontal plane (roll and pitch tolerance ± 2°).

In the flexible lower legform to bumper test, the bottom of the impactor (without launching/protection parts) shall be 75 ± 10 mm above the ground reference plane at the time of first contact with the bumper.
In the flexible lower legform to bumper test, the impact velocity of the impactor when striking the bumper shall be 11.1 ± 0.2 m/s.
In the upper legform to bumper test, the selected target points shall be in the bumper test area as defined in paragraph 3.10.

In the upper legform to bumper test, the direction of impact shall be parallel to the longitudinal axis of the vehicle with the axis of the upper legform vertical at the time of first contact, with a tolerance of ± 2°.

In the upper legform to bumper test, at the time of first contact the impactor centre line shall be vertically midway between the upper bumper reference line and the lower bumper reference line with a ± 10 mm tolerance, and laterally positioned at the selected impact location with a tolerance of ± 10 mm.
In the upper legform to bumper test, the impact velocity of the upper legform impactor when striking the bumper shall be 11.1 ± 0.2 m/s.
Where the upper grille/fascia lies within the child headform test area, child headform tests shall be made to the front structure within the boundaries defined in paragraph 3.13.
In the child headform test, no impact point shall be located so that the impactor will impact the test area with a glancing blow resulting in a more severe second impact outside the test area.

In the child headform test, selected impact points shall be, at the time of first contact, a minimum of 82.5 mm inside the side reference lines, forward of the WAD1700 line or a minimum of 82.5 mm forward of the bonnet rear reference line (whichever is most forward), and rearward of the WAD1000 line or a minimum of 82.5 mm rearward of the bonnet leading edge reference line (whichever is most rearward), measured with a flexible tape held tautly along the outer surface of the vehicle.
In the child headform test, the headform velocity at the time of impact shall be 9.7 ± 0.2 m/s.
In the child headform test, the direction of impact shall be in the longitudinal vertical plane of the vehicle at an angle of 50 ± 2° to the horizontal, downward and rearward.

If the pedestrian impact sensors form part of a Deployable Pedestrian Protection System (DPPS) and all prerequisites of Annex 1 are met, the vehicle shall be tested with the DPPS activated as intended for the entire headform test area.
For a vehicle with DPPS meeting the Annex 1 prerequisites, where HIT_d < TRT the headform test shall be performed dynamically.
For a vehicle with DPPS meeting the Annex 1 prerequisites, where HIT_d ≥ TRT the headform test may be performed either statically at a height no more than the deployed position or dynamically.
For a vehicle with DPPS, if any of the prerequisites of Annex 1 paragraphs 1.2 to 1.7 are not met, the vehicle shall be tested with the DPPS in the undeployed position.
For a vehicle with DPPS, the marking of the headform test areas shall always be done with the DPPS in the undeployed position, for static, dynamic or combined testing.
For a vehicle with DPPS, in the headform test for protection below the lower deployment threshold speed of the DPPS, the vehicle outer surface shall remain in the undeployed position.

For a vehicle with DPPS, the headform test for protection below the lower deployment threshold speed shall be performed according to paragraphs 7.2 to 7.4 of the Regulation with the impact speed set at 0.9 times the lower deployment threshold speed; the allocation of the HIC1700 and HIC1000 zones may differ from that of the nominal velocity (9.7 m/s) headform tests according to paragraph 5.2.4.
For a vehicle with DPPS, in the headform test below the lower deployment threshold speed the HIC shall comply with paragraph 5.2.3 of the Regulation.
For a vehicle with DPPS, the Human Body Models (HBM) used shall be qualified according to Addendum 5 of Mutual Resolution No. 1 (M.R.1).
For a vehicle with DPPS, the Head Impact Time (HIT) information shall be documented according to Annex 2 of the Regulation.

For a vehicle with DPPS tested in deployed static condition, the manufacturer-specified deployed position, maximum deployment height, sensing time (ST) and deployment time (DT) shall be verified by tracking means at the manufacturer-indicated reference points on the lifting devices, with a tolerance of -5 ms/+3 ms on the specified ST and ±20 per cent on the other specified values; if a measured value is within tolerance the manufacturer's value is used, otherwise the measured value is used.
For a vehicle with DPPS, the vehicle manufacturer shall specify the lowest speed of activation (lower deployment velocity threshold) of the DPPS.

For a vehicle with DPPS, for system deployment verification the DPPS sensing system shall activate in sensor activation tests with the FlexPLI, as specified in paragraph 6.3.1.1 of the Regulation, performed within the detection test area at the DPPS lower deployment velocity threshold.
For a vehicle with DPPS, a sensing system verification test with the FlexPLI shall be performed at nominal velocity (11.1 m/s) at the vehicle centreline (Y0).

For a vehicle with DPPS, where a sensing verification test is performed within the tolerances of Annex 1 paragraph 3 but below the lower deployment velocity threshold or outside the detection test area and the system does not deploy, the test must be repeated.

For a vehicle with DPPS, if the system is not activated during any of the sensing system verification tests, all headform tests shall be conducted in the undeployed position according to paragraphs 7.2 to 7.4 of the Regulation.

For a vehicle with DPPS, in sensing system verification tests with a stationary vehicle, the vehicle shall be set to the normal running condition specified by the manufacturer for a vehicle speed corresponding to the particular use case.
For a vehicle with DPPS, the Total Response Time (TRT) shall be confirmed using the FlexPLI at a vehicle speed of 11.1 m/s at the vehicle centreline (Y0).
For a vehicle with DPPS, the sensing time (ST) is measured either independently or during a TRT measurement test, at the vehicle speed specified in the Regulation and at the vehicle centreline (Y0).

For a vehicle with DPPS, if the measured ST is within a tolerance of -5 ms/+3 ms of the manufacturer-specified value, the manufacturer's value shall be used; otherwise the measured value shall be used for the test.
For a vehicle with DPPS tested dynamically, only the ST shall be verified.
For a vehicle with DPPS, in TRT/ST verification tests with a stationary vehicle, the vehicle shall be set to the normal running condition as specified by the manufacturer.

For a vehicle with DPPS, in headform tests at nominal velocity (9.7 m/s) the selection of impact points and the allocation of the HIC1700 and HIC1000 zones shall always be based on and related to the test area with undeployed DPPS.

For a vehicle with DPPS where the manufacturer opts for the static test procedure, the headform tests shall be performed statically only if all static test option conditions are fulfilled; if any of them is not met, the headform tests shall be performed dynamically.

For a vehicle with DPPS, where the manufacturer has demonstrated by numerical simulations on the deployed DPPS that HIT_d ≥ TRT for the smallest selected pedestrian stature as defined in Annex 2, all headform tests may be performed statically.
For a vehicle with DPPS tested statically, the vehicle outer surface shall represent the deployed position within the specified tolerances, while the resisting force is considered.

For a vehicle with DPPS tested statically where there is a time constraint on system stability and HIT_d ≥ TRT, the launching time of the headform impactor shall ensure that the system remains stable within ±10 per cent of the corresponding resisting force identified by the manufacturer.
For a vehicle with DPPS tested statically, it shall be ensured during the static tests that the resisting force of the DPPS is equivalent to the actual situation at HIT.
For a vehicle with DPPS tested statically, appropriate means (e.g. actuator surrogates) may be used to ensure that the corresponding resisting force of the DPPS is reached.
For a vehicle with DPPS tested statically, the headform test procedures of paragraphs 7.2 to 7.4 of the Regulation shall apply.

For a vehicle with DPPS using the combined test option at the manufacturer's choice, where the headform test area has sections with HIT_d < TRT and sections with HIT_d ≥ TRT, all test points forward of the corresponding WAD (HIT_d < TRT) shall be tested dynamically, while the remaining section of the headform test area may be tested statically.

For a vehicle with DPPS, the HBMs used for HIT determination shall comply with all requirements of Addendum 5 of M.R.1, and the qualification results shall be documented as specified in Addendum 5 of M.R.1.
For a vehicle with DPPS, only those HBM statures selected according to Annex 2 paragraph 2.2 shall be qualified.

For a vehicle with DPPS, the qualified pedestrian HBM shall be the very same model as used for HIT determination simulations, regarding HBM version, node position of every node, identical material (including fracture mode), contact and control cards and constraints, and, if available, identical initial element stresses/strains and initial contact penetrations/forces.

For a vehicle with DPPS, all qualification and HIT determination simulations shall be performed with consistent settings regarding solver version and type, time-step, time-step settings (initial and dynamic mass scaling), HBM-to-vehicle contact settings and control settings affecting the pedestrian model.

For a vehicle with DPPS, pedestrian models for HIT determination simulations shall be selected from the statures six-year-old (6YO), 5th percentile female (AF05), 50th percentile male (AM50) and 95th percentile male (AM95), in the position and stance defined in Addendum 5 of M.R.1.
For a vehicle with DPPS, in HIT determination simulations the pedestrian model shall be positioned with the head centre of gravity aligned with the vehicle centreline.

For a vehicle with DPPS, in HIT determination simulations the vehicle model shall be positioned so that the vehicle ground level is aligned with the ground level used in the qualification simulations.
For a vehicle with DPPS, in HIT determination simulations the HBM shall be exposed to a vertical acceleration field constituting gravitational loading as described in Addendum 5 of M.R.1.

For a vehicle with DPPS, in HIT determination simulations a local vehicle coordinate system shall be initially aligned with the global coordinate system of Addendum 5 of M.R.1 and connected to the vehicle model CoG.
For a vehicle with DPPS, the initial speed of the vehicle model in all HIT determination simulations shall be 40 km/h.
For a vehicle with DPPS, in HIT determination simulations the y and z motion of the vehicle model shall be constrained and the x-direction motion shall not be constrained.

For a vehicle with DPPS, the selected HBMs are those whose head hits the DPPS properly (head contacts the DPPS and, at that time, the x-coordinate of the head CoG lies between the smallest and largest x-coordinate of the DPPS at y=0); simulations with the next tallest HBM shall also be performed to prove that it does not hit the DPPS properly.
For a vehicle with DPPS, if only one HBM hits the DPPS properly, the next tallest HBM shall also belong to the selected HBMs.

For a vehicle with DPPS, each HIT determination simulation shall generate time history curves of x and z coordinates of HC and AC, x displacement of vehicle CoG, resultant HC acceleration, contact forces (vehicle–HBM without upper extremities, vehicle–head, total), total hourglass and internal energies, and mass increase, all plotted every 0.1 ms or less.
For a vehicle with DPPS, animations of each HIT determination simulation shall be generated with an output interval of 1 ms.
For a vehicle with DPPS, in each HIT determination simulation the contact force between HBM and vehicle shall be zero at simulation start.
For a vehicle with DPPS, in each HIT determination simulation the total energy shall remain constant within a 15 per cent tolerance.
For a vehicle with DPPS, in each HIT determination simulation the hourglass energy shall be ≤ 10 per cent of the total energy.
For a vehicle with DPPS, in each HIT determination simulation the artificial mass increase shall be less than 3 per cent.
For a vehicle with DPPS, in HIT determination simulations the coefficient of friction between vehicle and HBM shall be 0.3.

For a vehicle with DPPS, HIT shall be calculated as the time elapsed between the first contact of the HBM (neglecting forearms and hands) with the vehicle outer surface and the first contact of its head with the vehicle outer surface, first contact being the first time the contact force is non-zero; if this method is not applicable, an appropriate alternative method may be applied and shall be reported.

For a vehicle with DPPS, the WAD corresponding to HIT shall be determined by projecting the head CoG point (Xhead, 0, Zhead) at the time of first head contact with the DPPS orthogonally onto the surface of the undeployed vehicle (highest x value if multiple projection points) and computing the WAD of that point rounded to the nearest full millimetre.
For a vehicle with DPPS, if HIT_d ≥ TRT for all selected HBMs, HIT simulations on the undeployed DPPS are not required.
For a vehicle with DPPS, based on the HIT_d results of the deployed DPPS simulations, a WAD versus HIT_d graph using a linear regression line shall be plotted for comparison with TRT.

For a vehicle with DPPS, based on the HIT_s results of the undeployed DPPS simulations, a WAD versus HIT_s graph using a linear regression line shall be plotted, with the line extrapolated in both directions.

The vehicle (M1, maximum permissible mass ≤ 3,500 kg) fitted with the front bumper module (crossbeam with crash boxes, absorber, lower stiffener, fascia) shall be tested and approved in the Full Width Rigid Barrier test according to the method described in Annex 3. The test is satisfactory only if all the conditions of paragraphs 5.2.1 to 5.2.7 are satisfied at the same time.

The vehicle variant considered by the Technical Service as having the worst-case effect on the injury criteria of paragraph 5.2.1 shall be selected for the full width rigid barrier test, e.g. considering bumper variants such as crossbeam material and an EV charge-flap fitted or not fitted.

If an EV charging inlet is present (EV/PHEV variant with electric power train), the vehicle shall additionally meet the requirements of paragraph 5.2.8. At the manufacturer's request and after validation by the Technical Service, this may be shown by a separate impact test according to Annex 3 (except paragraphs 2, 5 and 6 of Annex 3), provided the electrical components do not influence the occupant protection performance defined in paragraphs 5.2.1 to 5.2.5.
In the frontal impact test, the head performance criterion (HPC) of the Hybrid III 50th percentile male dummy in the driver's seat shall not exceed 1000.

In the frontal impact test, the resultant head acceleration of the Hybrid III 50th percentile male dummy shall not exceed 80 g for more than 3 ms, calculated cumulatively and excluding rebound movement of the head.
In the frontal impact test, the axial tensile neck force of the Hybrid III 50th percentile male dummy shall not exceed 3.3 kN.
In the frontal impact test, the fore/aft shear forces at the head/neck interface of the Hybrid III 50th percentile male dummy shall not exceed 3.1 kN.
In the frontal impact test, the neck bending moment about the y axis of the Hybrid III 50th percentile male dummy shall not exceed 57 Nm in extension.
In the frontal impact test, the thorax compression criterion (ThCC) of the Hybrid III 50th percentile male dummy shall not exceed 42 mm.
In the frontal impact test, the viscous criterion (V*C) for the thorax of the Hybrid III 50th percentile male dummy shall not exceed 1.0 m/s.
In the frontal impact test, the femur force criterion (FFC) of the Hybrid III 50th percentile male dummy shall not exceed 9.07 kN.
In the frontal impact test, the head performance criterion (HPC) of the Hybrid III 5th percentile female dummy in the outboard passenger seat shall not exceed 1000.

In the frontal impact test, the resultant head acceleration of the Hybrid III 5th percentile female dummy shall not exceed 80 g for more than 3 ms, calculated cumulatively and excluding rebound movement of the head.
In the frontal impact test, the axial tensile neck force of the Hybrid III 5th percentile female dummy shall not exceed 2.9 kN.
In the frontal impact test, the fore/aft shear forces at the head/neck interface of the Hybrid III 5th percentile female dummy shall not exceed 2.7 kN.
In the frontal impact test, the neck bending moment about the y axis of the Hybrid III 5th percentile female dummy shall not exceed 57 Nm in extension.
In the frontal impact test of an M1 vehicle, the thorax compression criterion (ThCC) of the Hybrid III 5th percentile female dummy shall not exceed 34 mm.
In the frontal impact test, the viscous criterion (V*C) for the thorax of the Hybrid III 5th percentile female dummy shall not exceed 1.0 m/s.
In the frontal impact test, the femur force criterion (FFC) of the Hybrid III 5th percentile female dummy shall not exceed 7 kN.

After the frontal impact test, the residual steering wheel displacement measured at the centre of the steering wheel hub shall not exceed 80 mm in the upwards vertical direction. Vehicles meeting the steering wheel displacement requirements of either Regulation No. 12 or No. 94 are deemed to comply.

After the frontal impact test, the residual steering wheel displacement measured at the centre of the steering wheel hub shall not exceed 100 mm in the rearward horizontal direction. Vehicles meeting the steering wheel displacement requirements of either Regulation No. 12 or No. 94 are deemed to comply.

If the EV charging inlet is present and its circuit is high voltage: after the frontal impact test, the high voltage buses, including the coupling system for charging the REESS and the vehicle inlet in the bumper, shall meet at least one of the four criteria of paragraphs 5.2.8.1.1 to 5.2.8.1.4.2. If an automatic disconnect function or devices that divide the electric power train circuit are fitted, this applies to each disconnected or divided circuit after activation. The isolation resistance criterion (5.2.8.1.4) shall not apply if more than a single potential of a part of the high voltage bus is not protected to IPXXB.

If the EV charging inlet is present and its circuit is high voltage: when the crash test is performed with parts of the high voltage system not energized, protection against electrical shock for those parts shall be proved by either physical protection (5.2.8.1.3) or isolation resistance (5.2.8.1.4). This does not apply to a coupling system for charging the REESS that is not energized during driving condition.

If the EV charging inlet is present and its circuit is high voltage, and the absence-of-high-voltage criterion is used: the voltages Ub, U1 and U2 of the high voltage buses shall be ≤ 30 VAC or ≤ 60 VDC within 60 seconds after the impact, when measured in accordance with paragraph 2 of Annex 9.

If the EV charging inlet is present and its circuit is high voltage, and the low-electrical-energy criterion is used: the total energy (TE) on the high voltage buses shall be less than 0.2 J, measured according to paragraph 3 of Annex 9 with formula (a). Alternatively, TE may be calculated from the measured voltage Ub and the manufacturer-specified X-capacitor capacitance (Cx) according to formula (b).

If the EV charging inlet is present and its circuit is high voltage, and the low-electrical-energy criterion is used: the energy stored in the Y-capacitors (TEy1, TEy2) shall be less than 0.2 J. It is calculated from the measured voltages U1 and U2 between the high voltage buses and the electrical chassis and the manufacturer-specified Y-capacitor capacitance, according to formula (c) of paragraph 3 of Annex 9.

If the EV charging inlet is present and its circuit is high voltage, and the physical-protection criterion is used: protection degree IPXXB against direct contact with high voltage live parts shall be provided after the impact, assessed in accordance with paragraph 4 of Annex 9.

If the EV charging inlet is present and its circuit is high voltage, and the physical-protection criterion is used: the resistance between all exposed conductive parts of electrical protection barriers/enclosures and the electrical chassis shall be lower than 0.1 Ω with a current flow of at least 0.2 A. The resistance may be calculated from separately measured resistances of the relevant parts of the electric path. The requirement is satisfied if the galvanic connection is made by welding; otherwise, or in case of doubt, it shall be measured by one of the procedures in paragraph 4.1 of Annex 9.

If the EV charging inlet is present and its circuit is high voltage, and the physical-protection criterion is used: the resistance between any two simultaneously reachable exposed conductive parts of electrical protection barriers/enclosures less than 2.5 m apart shall be less than 0.2 Ω with a current flow of at least 0.2 A. The resistance may be calculated from separately measured resistances. The requirement is satisfied if the galvanic connection is made by welding; otherwise, or in case of doubt, it shall be measured by one of the procedures in paragraph 4.1 of Annex 9.

If the EV charging inlet is present and its circuit is high voltage, the isolation-resistance criterion is used, and the AC and DC high voltage buses are galvanically isolated from each other: the isolation resistance Ri between the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis, measured according to paragraph 5 of Annex 9, shall be at least 100 Ω/V of the working voltage for DC buses and at least 500 Ω/V of the working voltage for AC buses.

If the EV charging inlet is present and its circuit is high voltage, the isolation-resistance criterion is used, and the AC and DC high voltage buses are conductively connected: the isolation resistance between the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis, measured according to paragraph 5 of Annex 9, shall meet one of the following: (a) at least 500 Ω/V of the working voltage; (b) at least 100 Ω/V of the working voltage with the AC bus meeting the physical protection of paragraph 5.2.8.1.3; or (c) at least 100 Ω/V of the working voltage with the AC bus meeting the absence of high voltage of paragraph 5.2.8.1.1.

In the frontal impact test, the vehicle (fitted with the front bumper module) shall impact the barrier at a speed of 50 -0/+1 km/h; however, if the test was performed at a higher impact speed and the vehicle met the requirements, the test shall be considered satisfactory.

The frontal impact shall be made against a barrier consisting of a reinforced concrete block not less than 3 m wide in front, not less than 1.5 m high and weighing at least 70 metric tons, with a flat, vertical front face perpendicular to the axis of the run-up track covered with plywood boards 20 ± 2 mm thick in good condition (a structure on a steel plate at least 25 mm thick may be placed between the plywood and the barrier; a barrier with different characteristics may be used provided its impact surface area is greater than the frontal crash area of the vehicle and it gives equivalent results).

The vehicle shall reach the barrier on a course perpendicular to the collision wall, with a maximum lateral misalignment of ± 30 cm between the vertical median line of the front of the vehicle and the vertical median line of the collision wall.

The test vehicle shall be representative of the series production, shall include all the equipment normally fitted (including the front bumper module as produced) and shall be in normal running order; some components may be replaced by equivalent masses where this substitution clearly has no noticeable effect on the results measured.
For the frontal impact test, the mass of the vehicle submitted shall be the unladen kerb mass.

For vehicles with a high voltage electric power train (EV/PHEV variant with charging inlet in the bumper), the electric power train shall be energized during the test with or without the operation of the original electrical energy sources; by agreement between Technical Service and manufacturer, the test may be performed with all or parts of the electric power train not energized insofar as there is no negative influence on the test result, in which case for the parts not energized the protection against electrical shock shall be proved by either physical protection or isolation resistance and appropriate additional evidence.

If the EV charging inlet circuit integrated in the bumper is high voltage, then after the vehicle impact test the physical protection of its high voltage live parts shall meet paragraph 5.2.8.1.3. The physical protection is made up of the surrounding parts that remain after all parts that can be opened, disassembled or removed without tools have been opened or removed. To pass, the jointed test finger (Figure 3), inserted into any gap or opening with a test force of 10 N ± 10 per cent and articulated through every position up to 90 degrees at both joints, shall be unable to contact high voltage live parts.

If the EV charging inlet circuit integrated in the bumper is high voltage and the physical protection requirement is verified by a signal circuit between the jointed test finger and high voltage live parts, the lamp in the signal circuit shall not light.

If the EV charging inlet circuit integrated in the bumper is high voltage and has an electro-conductive enclosure or electrical protection barrier, the resistance R between that enclosure or barrier and the electrical chassis shall be less than 0.1 Ω. R is measured with a measurement current of at least 0.2 A, either with a resistance tester or with a DC power supply, voltmeter and ammeter (R = U / I).

If the EV charging inlet circuit integrated in the bumper is high voltage and post-crash electrical safety is demonstrated by voltage measurement, the high voltage bus voltages (Ub, U1, U2) shall be measured not earlier than 10 seconds and not later than 60 seconds after the impact. This does not apply if the test is performed with the electric power train not energized.

If the EV charging inlet circuit integrated in the bumper is high voltage and post-crash electrical safety is demonstrated by low electrical energy, the Total Energy (TE) shall be determined from measurements taken not earlier than 10 seconds and not later than 60 seconds after the impact. TE is either the integral of Ub x Ie from closing of switch S1 until Ub falls below 60 V DC, or TE = 0.5 x Cx x Ub² for X-capacitors, or TEy1 = 0.5 x Cy1 x U1² and TEy2 = 0.5 x Cy2 x U2² for Y-capacitors. This does not apply if the test is performed with the electric power train not energized.

If the EV charging inlet circuit integrated in the bumper is high voltage and post-crash electrical safety is demonstrated by isolation resistance, the isolation resistance of each high voltage bus (measured separately for each conductively isolated circuit) shall be determined from measurements made a minimum of 10 seconds after the impact. Any modifications made for the measurement shall not influence the test results.

The frontal offset deformable barrier test of the vehicle carrying the bumper module, carried out in accordance with Annex 3, shall be considered satisfactory only if all the conditions set out in paragraphs 5.2.1. to 5.2.7. are satisfied at the same time.

Vehicles equipped with an electric power train (e.g. EV variant with a high-voltage charging inlet behind the bumper flap) shall additionally meet the requirements of paragraph 5.2.8.; at the manufacturer's request and after validation by the Technical Service, this may be met by a separate impact test, provided the electrical components do not influence the occupant protection performance (paragraphs 5.2.1. to 5.2.5.). In that case paragraph 5.2.8. shall be checked by the Annex 3 methods except paragraphs 2., 5. and 6. of Annex 3, with a Hybrid III dummy fitted with a 45° angle installed in each front outboard seat.
The head performance criterion (HPC) recorded in accordance with Annex 8 on the dummies in the front outboard seats shall not exceed 1,000.
The resultant head acceleration of the dummies in the front outboard seats shall not exceed 80 g for more than 3 ms, calculated cumulatively and excluding rebound movement of the head.
The neck injury criteria (NIC) recorded on the dummies in the front outboard seats shall not exceed the values shown in Figure 1 (neck tension criterion) and Figure 2 (neck shear criterion).
The neck bending moment about the y axis of the dummies in the front outboard seats shall not exceed 57 Nm in extension.
The Thorax Compression Criterion (ThCC) of the dummies in the front outboard seats shall not exceed 42 mm.
The viscous criterion (V * C) for the thorax of the dummies in the front outboard seats shall not exceed 1,0 m/s.
The femur force criterion (FFC) of the dummies in the front outboard seats shall not exceed the force-time performance criterion shown in Figure 3.
The tibia compression force criterion (TCFC) of the dummies in the front outboard seats shall not exceed 8 kN.
The tibia index (TI), measured at the top and bottom of each tibia of the dummies in the front outboard seats, shall not exceed 1,3 at either location.
The movement of the sliding knee joints of the dummies in the front outboard seats shall not exceed 15 mm.

Following the test, the residual steering wheel displacement measured at the centre of the steering wheel hub shall not exceed 80 mm in the upwards vertical direction and 100 mm in the rearward horizontal direction.
During the frontal impact test no door shall open.
After the impact, the side doors shall be unlocked.

After the impact it shall be possible, without the use of tools except those necessary to support the weight of the dummy, to open at least one door per row of seats; where there is no such door, it shall be possible to evacuate all occupants by activating the seat displacement system if necessary (not applicable to convertibles whose top can be easily opened); this shall be assessed for all or the worst-case door configurations and for left- and right-hand drive vehicles, when applicable.
In the case of a vehicle propelled by liquid fuel (non-EV variant), no more than slight leakage of liquid from the fuel feed installation shall occur on collision.

In the case of a vehicle propelled by liquid fuel, if there is continuous leakage of liquid from the fuel-feed installation after the collision, the rate of leakage shall not exceed 30 g/min; where fuel mixes with other liquids that cannot easily be separated and identified, all liquids collected shall be taken into account.

If an HV vehicle inlet (coupling system for charging the REESS) is integrated behind the flap in the bumper module, after the impact the high voltage buses, including that coupling system, shall meet at least one of the four criteria of paragraphs 5.2.8.1.1 to 5.2.8.1.4.2; however, the isolation resistance criterion of 5.2.8.1.4 shall not apply if more than a single potential of a part of the high voltage bus is not protected under the conditions of protection degree IPXXB.

If an HV vehicle inlet is integrated in the bumper module and the crash test is performed with part(s) of the high voltage system not energized, protection against electrical shock for those parts shall be proved by paragraph 5.2.8.1.3 (physical protection) or 5.2.8.1.4 (isolation resistance), with the exception of any coupling system for charging the REESS which is not energized during driving condition.

If an HV vehicle inlet is integrated in the bumper module and the absence-of-high-voltage criterion is used, the voltages Ub, U1 and U2 of the high voltage buses shall be equal to or less than 30 VAC or 60 VDC within 60 s after the impact, measured in accordance with paragraph 2. of Annex 11.

If an HV vehicle inlet is integrated in the bumper module and the low-electrical-energy criterion is used, the Total Energy (TE) on the high voltage buses shall be less than 0.2 joules, measured according to paragraph 3. of Annex 11 with formula (a), or alternatively calculated from the measured voltage Ub and the manufacturer-specified X-capacitor capacitance (Cx) according to formula (b).

If an HV vehicle inlet is integrated in the bumper module and the low-electrical-energy criterion is used, the energy stored in the Y-capacitors (TEy1, TEy2) shall be less than 0.2 joules, calculated from the measured voltages U1 and U2 between the high voltage buses and the electrical chassis and the manufacturer-specified Y-capacitor capacitance according to formula (c) of paragraph 3. of Annex 11.

If an HV vehicle inlet is integrated in the bumper module and the physical-protection criterion is used, protection degree IPXXB against direct contact with high voltage live parts shall be provided after the impact, assessed in accordance with paragraph 4 of Annex 11.

If an HV vehicle inlet is integrated in the bumper module and the physical-protection criterion is used, the resistance between all exposed conductive parts of electrical protection barriers/enclosures and the electrical chassis shall be lower than 0.1 Ω with a current flow of at least 0.2 A (may be calculated from separately measured resistances; satisfied if the galvanic connection is welded; otherwise measured per paragraph 4.1. of Annex 11).

If an HV vehicle inlet is integrated in the bumper module and the physical-protection criterion is used, the resistance between any two simultaneously reachable exposed conductive parts of electrical protection barriers/enclosures less than 2.5 m from each other shall be less than 0.2 Ω with a current flow of at least 0.2 A (may be calculated from separately measured resistances; satisfied if the galvanic connection is welded; otherwise measured per paragraph 4.1. of Annex 11).

If an HV vehicle inlet is integrated in the bumper module, the isolation-resistance criterion is used and the AC and DC high voltage buses are galvanically isolated from each other, the isolation resistance Ri between the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis, measured per paragraph 5. of Annex 11, shall be at least 100 Ω/V of the working voltage for DC buses and at least 500 Ω/V of the working voltage for AC buses.

If an HV vehicle inlet is integrated in the bumper module, the isolation-resistance criterion is used and the AC and DC high voltage buses are conductively connected, the isolation resistance between the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis, measured per paragraph 5. of Annex 11, shall be at least 500 Ω/V of the working voltage, or at least 100 Ω/V of the working voltage with the AC bus meeting the physical protection of paragraph 5.2.8.1.3 or the absence of high voltage of paragraph 5.2.8.1.1.

Every vehicle approved under this Regulation, including its bumper module front structure, shall be manufactured so as to conform to the vehicle type approved and satisfy the requirements of paragraphs 5. and 6.

For the frontal collision test, the vehicle (including the front bumper module) shall impact a barrier whose front face is a deformable structure as defined in Annex 9 of UN R94. The deformable face shall be perpendicular within ±1° to the direction of travel of the test vehicle and secured to a mass of not less than 7 x 10^4 kg.

The barrier shall be oriented so that the vehicle's first contact with it is on the steering-column side. Where the test can be carried out with either a right-hand or a left-hand drive vehicle, it shall be carried out with the less favourable hand of drive as determined by the Technical Service.
In the frontal collision test, the vehicle shall overlap the barrier face by 40 per cent ± 20 mm.

Vehicle speed at the moment of impact shall be 56 -0/+1 km/h. However, if the test was performed at a higher impact speed and the vehicle met the requirements, the test shall be considered satisfactory.

The test vehicle shall be representative of series production, including the series front bumper module, and shall include all the equipment normally fitted and be in normal running order. Some components may be replaced by equivalent masses where this substitution clearly has no noticeable effect on the results measured under paragraph 6 of Annex 3.
For the frontal collision test, the mass of the vehicle submitted shall be the unladen kerb mass.

If a high-voltage vehicle inlet is integrated behind the charging flap in the bumper module and the test is performed with that part of the electric power train not energized (permitted by agreement between Technical Service and manufacturer, insofar as there is no negative influence on the test result), protection against electrical shock for the non-energized parts shall be proved by either physical protection or isolation resistance, together with appropriate additional evidence.

In the simplified (trolley) test according to Annex 7, the structure tested shall be representative of the series production of the vehicles concerned. Some components may be replaced or removed where this clearly has no effect on the test results.

In the simplified test according to Annex 7, the deceleration curve of the structure during the impact phase shall be such that the 'variation of speed in relation to time' curve obtained by integration differs at no point by more than ±1 m/s from the reference curve of the vehicle concerned. That reference curve is obtained from the full-scale barrier test. The reference curve may be displaced along the time axis to bring the structure velocity inside the corridor.

The simplified test may be performed by a method other than deceleration of a trolley, provided that the method complies with the ±1 m/s speed-variation corridor requirement of paragraph 1.6 of Annex 7.

If an HV vehicle inlet (AC and/or DC) is integrated behind the charging flap in the bumper module: after the vehicle impact test, with any parts surrounding the high voltage components that can be opened, disassembled or removed without tools taken away, the jointed test finger (Figure 3) inserted into any gaps or openings of the remaining physical protection with a test force of 10 N ± 10 per cent, and both joints rotated progressively up to 90 degrees into every possible position, shall be unable to contact high voltage live parts (requirement of paragraph 5.2.8.1.3.).

If an HV vehicle inlet is integrated in the bumper module and protection against direct contact is verified by a signal circuit (low-voltage supply of 40 V to 50 V in series with a lamp) between the jointed test finger and the high voltage live parts, the lamp shall not light.

If an HV vehicle inlet is integrated in the bumper module: the electric resistance between the electrical chassis and any electro-conductive enclosure/electrical protection barrier of the high voltage parts, measured after the impact with a measurement current of at least 0.2 A (resistance tester with resolution 0.01 Ω or less, or DC power supply, voltmeter and ammeter with R = U / I), shall be less than 0.1 Ω.

If an HV vehicle inlet is integrated in the bumper module and compliance is shown by voltage measurement: the high voltage bus voltages (Ub, U1, U2) shall be measured not earlier than 10 seconds and not later than 60 seconds after the impact; this procedure does not apply if the test is performed with the electric power train not energized.

If an HV vehicle inlet is integrated in the bumper module and compliance is shown by low electrical energy: the Total Energy (TE) of the high voltage bus shall be determined from 10 to 60 seconds after the impact, either by integrating Ub x Ie through a discharge resistor from closing switch S1 until Ub falls below the high voltage threshold of 60 V DC, or as TE = 0.5 x Cx x Ub² (X-capacitors) and TEy1 = 0.5 x Cy1 x U1², TEy2 = 0.5 x Cy2 x U2² (Y-capacitors) where the capacitances are specified by the manufacturer; this procedure does not apply if the test is performed with the electric power train not energized.

If an HV vehicle inlet is integrated in the bumper module: the isolation resistance shall be determined for each high voltage bus of the vehicle (including the inlet), either by measurement or by calculation from the measurement values of each part or component unit of the high voltage bus, with all measurements made a minimum of 10 s after the impact.
If an HV vehicle inlet is integrated in the bumper module and the high voltage buses are conductively isolated from each other, the isolation resistance shall be measured for each electrical circuit.

If an HV vehicle inlet is integrated in the bumper module and the isolation resistance is measured with an external DC voltage source, it shall be measured between the live parts and the electrical chassis applying a DC voltage of at least half the working voltage of the high voltage bus; components that cannot withstand the working voltage of the entire circuit may be disconnected and measured separately applying at least half of their own working voltage.

If the bumper sensors (ultrasonic PDC, radar, radar/LIDAR and/or camera) serve as ACPE forward detection means: the ACPE shall be able to limit unintended acceleration of the vehicle when an accelerator control misapplication by the driver has been detected, at least when an obstacle exists in front of the vehicle and the driving direction is selected to be forward.

If the bumper sensors serve as ACPE forward detection means: if the ACPE is not ready to perform an intervention 6 seconds after the initiation of the vehicle powertrain, this status shall be indicated to the driver, and this information shall exist until the system has been successfully initialised.

If the bumper sensors serve as ACPE forward detection means: the ACPE shall limit vehicle acceleration to prevent or mitigate a collision with an obstacle located between 1.0 m and 1.5 m in front of the vehicle, in the vehicle path, at the time the accelerator control is applied, provided: the road is flat, horizontal and dry affording good adhesion; the weather does not affect vehicle performance (e.g. no storm, not below 0 °C); the vehicle state allows the acceleration inhibition (tyres, brakes, no severe uneven load, no trailer, mass between maximum mass and mass in running order, powertrain management operational); ambient illumination is at least 1000 lux with no extreme blinding of the sensors (e.g. direct blinding sunlight, highly radar-reflective environment); the target vehicle is not extreme in Radar Cross Section or shape/silhouette (e.g. below the fifth percentile of RCS of all M1 vehicles); no significant weather conditions affect sensing (e.g. heavy rain, dense fog, snow, dirt); no overhead obstructions are close to the vehicle; the obstacle is stationary, unobstructed and clearly separated from other objects; the lateral offset between obstacle and vehicle centrelines is not more than 0.2 m; the travel direction is straight; and the obstacle is an M1 vehicle or a wall-like structure at least 2.0 m wide and 1.0 m high.

If the bumper sensors serve as ACPE forward detection means: when conditions deviate from those listed in paragraph 5.1.5 (e.g. sensing conditions, weather, illumination), the system shall not deactivate or unreasonably switch the control strategy; this shall be demonstrated by the manufacturer in accordance with Annex 3 and may be followed by Technical Service testing in deviating conditions.

If the bumper sensors serve as ACPE forward detection means: in the case that a collision is not prevented, the collision speed shall be no greater than 8 km/h higher than the vehicle speed at the point where the triggering conditions of paragraph 5.1.2 are met.

If the bumper sensors serve as ACPE forward detection means: in the case that a collision is not prevented, the collision speed shall not be greater than 70 % of the speed the vehicle would have had in the same position and circumstances without ACPE intervention; however, for vehicles that do not exceed 8 km/h without ACPE in the test scenarios but cannot achieve a 30 % speed reduction due to a low engine power to test mass ratio, the speed reduction shall be at least 15 %.

If the bumper sensors serve as ACPE forward detection means: during any intervention the vehicle acceleration shall continue to be limited by the ACPE; the intervention may be ended when the obstacle is no longer detected or the driver has interrupted the function.

If the bumper sensors serve as ACPE forward detection means: the effectiveness of the ACPE shall not be adversely affected by magnetic or electrical fields, demonstrated by fulfilling the technical requirements and respecting the transitional provisions of the 06 or later series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 10.
If the bumper sensors serve as ACPE forward detection means: conformity with the safety aspects of electronic control systems shall be shown by meeting the requirements of Annex 3.

If the bumper sensors serve as ACPE forward detection means: a failure warning as specified in paragraph 5.4.3 shall be given to the driver when there is a failure in the ACPE (including its detection sensors) that prevents the requirements of the Regulation being met.

If the bumper sensors serve as ACPE forward detection means: it is not required to provide a failure warning signal to indicate that the ACPE is temporarily not available, for example due to inclement weather conditions.
If the bumper sensors serve as ACPE forward detection means: there shall not be an appreciable time interval between each ACPE self-check.

If the bumper sensors serve as ACPE forward detection means: in the case of an electrically detectable failure there shall not be a delay in illuminating the failure warning signal; however, if the vehicle speed is greater than 10 km/h when the failure is detected, the warning may be suppressed until the vehicle speed is next below 10 km/h.

If the bumper sensors serve as ACPE forward detection means: a failure warning shall also be given to the driver in the case of a detected non-electrical failure condition (e.g. sensor blindness or sensor misalignment), unless a deactivation warning is given as per paragraph 5.2.3.1.3.
If the bumper sensors serve as ACPE forward detection means: the ACPE performance tests are performed at an ambient temperature between 0 °C and 45 °C.
If the bumper sensors serve as ACPE forward detection means: the ACPE performance tests are performed with natural ambient illumination homogeneous in the test area and in excess of 1000 lux.

If the bumper sensors serve as ACPE forward detection means: at the request of the manufacturer and with the agreement of the Technical Service, tests may be conducted under deviating (suboptimal) conditions, e.g. on a not dry surface or below the specified minimum ambient temperature, whilst the performance requirements are still to be met.

If the bumper sensors serve as ACPE forward detection means and if requested by the vehicle manufacturer: the vehicle may be driven a maximum of 100 km on a mixture of urban and rural roads with other traffic and roadside furniture to initialise the sensor system before testing.

If the bumper sensors serve as ACPE forward detection means: the ACPE shall detect, in the vehicle detection tests, a target that is a regular high-volume series production passenger car of Category M1 or a soft target representative of a passenger vehicle in terms of its identification characteristics applicable to the ACPE sensor system according to ISO 19206-1:2018 or ISO 19206-3:2021 at the choice of the manufacturer.

If the bumper sensors serve as ACPE forward detection means: the accelerator control misapplication test shall be performed in the forward direction with and without an expected ACPE intervention, with the vehicle at least 1.0 m (+0.1 m) and 1.5 m (-0.1 m) from the target at the start, a lateral offset between target and vehicle centrelines of 0.0 m to 0.2 m, steering in neutral, and the triggering conditions of paragraph 5.1.2 achieved before the vehicle reaches 0.5 km/h.

If the bumper sensors serve as ACPE forward detection means: forward driving direction, distance to target 1.0 m (tolerance +0.1 m longitudinal, ±0.2 m lateral), target present: the ACPE shall intervene.

If the bumper sensors serve as ACPE forward detection means: forward driving direction, distance to speed measuring point 1.0 m (tolerance +0.1 m longitudinal), no target present: test without ACPE intervention or with ACPE deactivated (may be combined with other no-target tests).

If the bumper sensors serve as ACPE forward detection means: forward driving direction, distance to target 1.5 m (tolerance -0.1 m longitudinal, ±0.2 m lateral), target present: the ACPE shall intervene.

If the bumper sensors serve as ACPE forward detection means: forward driving direction, distance to speed measuring point 1.5 m (tolerance -0.1 m longitudinal), no target present: test without ACPE intervention or with ACPE deactivated (may be combined with other no-target tests).

Where the bumper sensors (ultrasonic PDC, radar, radar/LIDAR, camera) and their harness form part of the ACPE 'The System', The System shall respect, under non-fault and fault conditions, all the appropriate performance requirements specified elsewhere in UN R175, and the disclosed information shall show this.

Where the bumper sensors form part of the ACPE 'The System', The System shall be designed to operate in such a way that it does not induce safety critical risks, and the disclosed information shall show this.

Where the bumper sensors form part of the ACPE 'The System', a documentation package shall be provided which gives access to the basic design of The System and the means by which it is linked to other vehicle systems or by which it directly controls output variables.
The function(s) of the ACPE 'The System' and the safety concept, as laid down by the manufacturer, shall be explained in the documentation.

For periodic technical inspections, the documentation shall describe how the current operational status of the ACPE 'The System' (including the bumper sensors where they form part of it) can be checked.

A description shall be provided which gives a simple explanation of all the control functions of the ACPE 'The System' and the methods employed to achieve the objectives, including a statement of the mechanism(s) by which control is exercised.
Any described function of the ACPE 'The System' that can be over-ridden shall be identified and a further description of the changed rationale of the function's operation provided.

A list of all input and sensed variables of the ACPE 'The System' (e.g. signals of the bumper ultrasonic, radar, LIDAR and camera sensors where used) shall be provided and the working range of these defined.

A list of all output variables controlled by the ACPE 'The System' shall be provided, indicating in each case whether the control is direct or via another vehicle system, and the range of control exercised on each such variable shall be defined.
Limits defining the boundaries of functional operation of the ACPE 'The System' shall be stated where appropriate to system performance.

A list shall be provided collating all the units of the ACPE 'The System' (including bumper sensors where they form part of it) and mentioning the other vehicle systems needed to achieve the control function, together with an outline schematic showing these units in combination with both the equipment distribution and the interconnections made clear.

The function of each unit of the ACPE 'The System' (e.g. each bumper sensor used as forward detection means) shall be outlined and the signals linking it with other units or other vehicle systems shall be shown, e.g. by a labelled block diagram or other schematic or a description aided by such a diagram.

Interconnections within the ACPE 'The System' shall be shown by a circuit diagram for the electric transmission links (e.g. the bumper wiring harness), by a piping diagram for pneumatic or hydraulic equipment and by a simplified diagrammatic layout for mechanical linkages.
The transmission links both to and from other systems shall also be shown for the ACPE 'The System'.
There shall be a clear correspondence between the transmission links of the ACPE 'The System' and the signals and/or operating data carried between units.

Priorities of signals and/or operating data on multiplexed data paths of the ACPE 'The System' shall be stated wherever priority may be an issue affecting performance or safety as far as UN R175 is concerned.

Each unit of the ACPE 'The System' (including each bumper sensor forming part of it) shall be clearly and unambiguously identifiable (e.g. by marking for hardware and marking or software output for software content) to provide corresponding hardware and documentation association.
Where functions are combined within a single unit or single computer but shown in multiple blocks in the block diagram, only a single hardware identification marking shall be used for that unit.
The manufacturer shall, by the use of the unit identification, affirm that the equipment supplied conforms to the corresponding document.

The unit identification shall define the hardware and software version, and where the software changes such as to alter the function of the unit as far as UN R175 is concerned, the identification shall also be changed.

The manufacturer shall provide a statement which affirms that the strategy chosen to achieve the ACPE 'The System' objectives will not, under non-fault conditions, prejudice the safe operation of the vehicle.

In respect of software employed in the ACPE 'The System' (including sensor software where the sensors form part of it), the outline architecture shall be explained and the design methods and tools used shall be identified.
The manufacturer shall show evidence of the means by which the realisation of the system logic of the ACPE 'The System' was determined during the design and development process.

The manufacturer shall provide an explanation of the design provisions built into the ACPE 'The System' so as to generate safe operation under fault conditions (e.g. fall-back to a partial system, change-over to a back-up system, removal of the high level function).

In case of a failure of the ACPE 'The System' (e.g. a failure or blockage of a bumper sensor forming part of it), the driver shall be warned, for example by warning signal or message display, and unless the system is deactivated by the driver (e.g. ignition switch to 'off' or switching off the function by a special switch), the warning shall be present as long as the fault condition persists.

The documentation shall be supported by an analysis which shows, in overall terms, how the ACPE 'The System' will behave on the occurrence of any individual hazard or fault (e.g. of a bumper sensor or harness) which will have a bearing on vehicle control performance or safety, and the chosen analytical approach(es) shall be established, maintained and made open for inspection at type approval.
The safety approach at concept (vehicle) level shall include consideration of interactions with other vehicle systems and shall be based on a Hazard / Risk analysis appropriate to system safety.
The safety approach at system level shall be based on a Failure Mode and Effect Analysis (FMEA), a Fault Tree Analysis (FTA) or any similar process appropriate to system safety.

Validation plans and results shall be available for the ACPE 'The System', the validation using, for example, Hardware in the Loop (HIL) testing, vehicle on-road operational testing or any means appropriate for validation.

The documentation shall itemize the parameters being monitored in the ACPE 'The System' and shall set out, for each fault condition, the warning signal to be given to the driver and/or to service/technical inspection personnel.

The documentation shall describe the measures in place to ensure the ACPE 'The System' does not prejudice the safe operation of the vehicle when its performance is affected by environmental conditions, e.g. climatic, temperature, dust ingress, water ingress, ice packing (relevant to the bumper sensors and, if fitted, the heated sensor window).

The ACPE 'The System' shall operate as declared by the manufacturer when selected functions are tested under non-fault conditions, including, for complex electronic systems, scenarios in which a declared function is overridden.

When the reaction of the ACPE 'The System' is checked under the influence of a failure in any individual unit (simulated by applying corresponding output signals to electrical units or mechanical elements), the verification results shall correspond with the documented summary of the failure analysis, to a level of overall effect such that the safety concept and execution are confirmed as adequate, including aspects of vehicle controllability and user information (HMI).
